findings.title: A standing last-stand ASK suppresses the retreat on every re-attack: the marshal is ground to nothing over 11 battles and DESTROYED, never asked, never captured
findings._corrected: W6-7's fate arm (`_check_marshal_fate`, combat_executor.py:3195) fires on EVERY forced retreat with no guard for an already-standing `pending_interrupt`. For an aggressive player marshal whose only exit is tier-5 at-war soil (`desperation_only`, :3233-3240) it sets `pending_interrupt=last_stand` (:3313-3328) and returns a message, which `_apply_forced_retreat_or_break` treats as 'retreat consumed' (:3484-3486) — so the marshal does NOT move. The victor then advances INTO his province because `can_advance = victor == marshal.name` ignores that the defender still stands (:6689-6698, 'MOVING Mack: Milan -> Piedmont' in the console with `defender_fled=False`). Every co-located enemy corps is then FORCED to attack him by the P0 engagement rung (enemy_ai.py:1615 weakest-enemy, :1674 attack) before anything else, and each new attack re-runs the fate arm, re-raises the same ask and again suppresses the retreat. Verified by running: the driver reproduction of audit-latewar-t20 shows Massena at Piedmont, `pending_interrupt=last_stand`, `retreating=False`, strength 21,067 → 8,848 (turn 25) → 702 (turn 26) → 58 (turn 27) → `[DESTROYED] Massena reduced to rubble (32 -> 0)` (server_console.log:5026), `fallen_marshals={'Massena': {turn 28, cause 'battle'}}`. Eleven battles, zero prisoners, zero last stand, and the digest never showed the question (see the harness finding). The non-aggressive arm (:3375) rolls and either retreats or is captured in ONE battle; the ask arm is the only path that leaves a man standing to be shot by the rest of the phase.

findings.player_consequence: The player's aggressive marshal (Massena, Ney, Lannes, Murat) is 'CORNERED — awaiting your word' during the enemy phase, but the enemy phase does not wait: every other adjacent enemy corps attacks him in the same phase, so a 15,000-man corps is destroyed piecemeal before the player can type an answer. He gets neither the +25% last stand nor a capture (which would have returned 50% of his men to the manpower pool and made him ransomable) — the two outcomes the W6-7 promise names. The flagship digest shows the same shape for Lannes (turn 13: 3,673/2,654/1,056/496 in one phase, DESTROYED at Munich turn 15, digest lines 214-217, 255).

findings.title: Accepting the AI's own incoming settlement offer stages a review the AI itself rejects — the coalition-peace route is a dead affordance
findings._corrected: `accept_settlement_offer` re-scores the OFFERING courts as the accepting side of a package France 'proposed' (settlement_offers.py:2696-2716 forwards the terms with `actor_nation=player`, deliberately dropping the offer's `proposer_side`), and the settlement scorer charges a white/status-quo peace a −10 tier base (settlement_scoring.py:466-471, 731-780) plus agenda −8, so no offering court reaches the 50 threshold and the staged `settlement_confirm` arrives with `ratify_blocked_reason` and NO ratify option. Verified by running in four states: fresh 1805 boot at turn 4 (Britain's first offer: Austria −1/50, Britain −4/50, Russia −4/50, top blocker `settlement_tier_legitimacy`), historical seed turn 15 with France ahead (+13 stored; Austria 2/50, Britain 2/50, Russia 'no terms can move them' because Russia had ALREADY made peace at turn 12 yet is still in the turn-3 offer's `covered_enemy_participants`), the late-war fixture turn 23 (Switzerland's own white peace: Switzerland 5/50 'the terms claim a victory the field has not delivered') and turn 24 (Britain's offer while France is at −78: 'cannot be ratified now: the terms claim a victory the field has not delivered'). The producer never scores its own package (`_emit_settlement_offer_for_war`, ai_diplomacy.py:3541 — zero acceptance calls in the body, grep-verified). The accept also pops and removes the offer BEFORE staging (settlement_offers.py:2714-2716), so the dead review is the offer's end. Every route the game names for a coalition peace lands here: the alliance-paradox block says 'Settle the war jointly at the settlement table' (diplomatic_dialogue.py:868-872), `request terms` says 'Their terms are already on the desk, Sire — answer the offer in the mailbox' (display_names.py:877-884; audit-latewar-t20 T21 verbatim), and a granted terms request emits through the same producer (settlement_routes.py:260-326).

findings.fix_shape: ONE seam: the accept branch of `handle_incoming_settlement_offer_action` (settlement_offers.py:2696-2745). The offering side's consent is given by construction — stage the review with the OFFER's own `proposer_side`/courts marked pre-consenting (or ratify the offered package directly through `settlement_ratify` on the player's confirm), and only pop/remove the offer after staging succeeds. Optionally have `_emit_settlement_offer_for_war` pre-score its package (the EWC-F1 shape) so the AI never offers what its own scorer rejects.

findings.title: Accepting the settlement offer on screen pops it BEFORE staging, so the next queued offer (another war) trips the cross-war collision and the offer the player clicked is destroyed
findings._corrected: The accept branch removes the pending entry and pops the dialogue first (settlement_offers.py:2714-2716), `dialogue_manager.pop()` promotes the next queued item (dialogue_manager.py:347-351, 779-793), and only THEN `stage_settlement_confirm` runs its SC-26 collision check against `_mounted_settlement_dialogue` = the CURRENT dialogue (settlement_staging.py:3388-3405; settlement_routes.py:359-371, whose docstring says queued items must NOT count). With Britain's war_1 offer current and Switzerland's war_2 offer queued, accepting the offer ON SCREEN returns `cross_war_settlement_collision` — 'the settlement of war_2 is already on the table; resolve it before opening a separate review for war_1' — naming an offer the player has never seen, and Britain's offer is gone (current becomes Switzerland's). The archived late-war digest shows exactly this at T23, and the raw war ids leak into the sentence.

With Britain's war_1 offer current and Switzerland's war_2 offer queued, accepting the offer ON SCREEN returns `cross_war_settlement_collision` — 'the settlement of war_2 is already on the table; resolve it before opening a separate review for war_1' — naming an offer the player has never seen, and Britain's offer is gone (current becomes Switzerland's). findings.player_consequence: A losing France (13 provinces, Paget walking the homeland) clicks Review on the coalition leader's peace offer and is told a different, invisible war is 'on the table'; the offer disappears; the collision copy prints `war_2`/`war_1`. Peace with the court that is actually beating France cannot be accepted until the unrelated rebel war's offer is dealt with — and that one is itself un-ratifiable (FA-3).

findings.title: An end-turn-only stretch never delivers the marshal petition, and the undelivered card starves Fontainebleau and every later petition
findings._corrected: `_apply_command_popup_contract` (main.py:1353-1361) calls `_include_popup_passthroughs` only when the response has NO `enemy_phase`, so the end-turn response never carries `marshal_petition`; the card waits for the player's next non-end-turn `/command`. The client's post-enemy-phase tail (`_on_enemy_phase_dismissed` main.gd:4340-4392 → `_return_control_to_player` main.gd:2261-2280) polls only `GET /pending_redemption` (main.py:3625-3626) — there is no `/pending_petition` poll and no GET route delivers `pending_marshal_petition` (`_fill_popup_keys_without_draining`, main.py:1509, sets the key to None). While the card sits, `_push_petition` returns BLOCKED for any OTHER petition (jealousy.py:1861-1862) and `check_fontainebleau` returns without stamping (jealousy.py:2269) — so the collective petition is unreachable for as long as the player only presses End Turn. Verified by running the in-process probe: `pending_marshal_petition=jealousy_confrontation` from world turn 5 through turn 24, `jealousy_confrontations_seen` frozen at ['Murat|Ney@L0'], every end-turn response `popups: []`; five marshals eroding from turn 10 (≥ `FONTAINEBLEAU_MIN_ERODING`=3, jealousy.py:114) yet `fontainebleau_last_turn` stayed −999 for 24 turns; Davout's grievances toward Murat (turns 5, 8, 11) never got a card. Control run: with one `status` command per turn the confrontation arrived on the `status` response at turn 5. Verified by opening the archives: audit-ambient40 (40 turns) has zero marshal_petition popups (meta.json popups=14 = 14 LETTER rows), and in audit-flagship-mock the first petition rides `Davout, attack Mack` (digest.md:27-30), not `end turn`.

findings.title: A sentence containing "next turn" advances the turn irreversibly — including a QUESTION ("what happens next turn")
findings._corrected: The mock chain's end_turn arm is a bare substring test that sits above every order verb: llm_client.py:1411 `elif "end turn" in command_lower or "end_turn" in command_lower or "next turn" in command_lower: action = "end_turn"` (verified by opening). A qualifier on an order ("…next turn", "…and end turn") therefore becomes the end-turn command itself, and meta_executor.py:164-167 only WARNS about unused AP ("PT-6: Warn about unused AP (informational — turn still ends)", verified by opening). findings.amendment: Downgraded P1->P2 on 2026-09-02 after an owner challenge, upheld. (a) 'forfeits all 4 AP' was wrong: actions_remaining resets to calculate_max_actions() at every turn start (world_state.py:9608), so AP never carry over — nothing is banked or stolen and there is no cheat vector. The fix must NOT queue the order: no deferred-order system exists and inventing one would hand out free actions. (b) 'Davout, attack next turn' is not a sentence a real player types, and the substring arm is deliberate synonym handling the client gate was widened to mirror (main.gd:1292-1302, Aug 30 2026). WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured 2026-09-02 on the 1805 boot via POST /command: 'what happens next turn' -> turn 1->2 with the enemy phase run; likewise 'we will decide next turn' and 'Ney, hold here and attack next turn'; but 'what should we do next turn?' and 'can Davout attack next turn?' hit the help arm and hold the turn. The defect is that a NON-COMMAND advances the turn irreversibly with no confirmation unless envoys are lapsing, and inconsistently — a question mark saves you, its absence does not.

findings.title: Deferral orders launch the attack NOW — "Ney, delay the attack" / "attack Mack later" / "wait for Davout then attack Mack" all fight a battle immediately
findings._corrected: PARSE-NEG's negation guard (clause_guards.py:77-104 `_NEGATION_MARKER_RE`, verified by opening) knows never/do not/refrain/rather than/instead of/without/avoid but no deferral verb (delay, postpone, defer, put off, hold off) or deferral adverb (later, for now); `_REFUSING_CONDITION_WORDS` (:148) has if/when/once/after but not later/next turn. So "delay the attack" survives to the chain, where `attack` (llm_client.py:1442) outranks `wait` (:1475). For "wait for Davout then attack Mack", parser.py:53-66 `_ATTACK_ON_ARRIVAL_TAIL_RE` deliberately refuses to split a tail that starts with attack, so the whole sentence is one parse and attack wins. With no named foe, the guessed-target arm (combat_executor.py:172-200, `auto_resolved=True`) PROCEEDS with a disclosure rather than refusing.

findings.title: P4.25 garrison assault prices the garrison and ignores the field army standing in the province (the Munich suicide loop)
findings._corrected: `_find_garrison_attack` (backend/ai/enemy_ai.py:3502-3571) scans adjacent garrisoned provinces and gates the assault on `marshal.strength / garrison_effective` (line 3558, garrison x terrain x fort) — it checks garrison size, controller, war state, the crossing gate and terrain, but NEVER whether enemy marshals stand in the target region. Its siblings do: P4.5 skips a defended province at :3447 and P3.7 checks `defenders` before the garrison arm at :3175. The executor then resolves the 'garrison assault' as a field battle against whoever is in the region (combat_executor.py:4818 `get_enemy_at_location_for_nation(resolved_target)`), so a cautious 29k corps that computed 2.32:1 against a 10k garrison walks into 53k Frenchmen at 0.5:1. The futility brake does not guard P4.25 (WO-3 records it was consciously not built) and the CA9-N6 field-pricing fix landed on P0/P4 only, so the same marshal repeats the assault every recovery cycle. The sibling seam in P7.5's stagnation arms (:3842-3876, ratio against ONE marshal, no futility, no crossing gate) carries the same defender-blindness and should be swept in the same slice.

findings.title: The driver's refused-choice memory turns a transient stale_dialogue refusal into a permanent ban — four flagship offers were never answered and an accept-policy run answered a settlement with 'request revision'
findings._corrected: `Answerer.scan` memorizes ANY reply with success False under the dialogue's identity (`tools/playtest_driver.py:932-935`) and `_dialogue_choice` never re-offers it. findings.title: A persistent settlement offer starves every answer behind it: France's own peace overture returns a COUNTER-OFFER that is queued unseen and lapses at the next end turn — 3 DP per turn, no popup, no cooldown
findings._corrected: `incoming_settlement_offer` is persistent (mailbox priority 2, dialogue_manager.py:183-193) and `_promote` sorts by priority (:779-793), so while one sits in the slot every current-turn item pushed behind it — `counter_offer_response` (priority 3) and AI `incoming_proposal` letters — never becomes current, never writes `incoming_proposal_popup` (the IGR-F conditional write, ai_diplomacy.py:2057-2063; world_state.py:10129-10130), and is lapsed by `lapse_pending_offers` at the start of the next end_turn whether or not it was ever shown (dialogue_manager.py:558-580). The COUNTER_OFFER branch of `_process_proposal_in_transit` writes no `proposal_result_popup` and no cooldown (world_state.py:10060-10132 vs the REJECT branch :10194-10201), and the dispatch line is contentless ('Talleyrand returns from {nation} with a response.', dispatch.py:3803). In the archived propose campaign this happened on SEVEN consecutive turns (13,15,17,18,19,20,21: 'Talleyrand departs for the Austria court… (3 DP spent)' with no result ever shown) because Britain's turn-3 settlement offer held the slot for 21 turns.

Austria's actual answer — 'France offers 1000 gold' as a counter — is visible only as a mailbox badge for one turn and then silently lapses; no cooldown fires, so the player can (and the archived run did) repeat the same futile overture every turn.

Expect a response by next turn. (3 DP spent)` with no `Austria has rejected/accepted` line until turn 22).

findings.title: A queued proposal's popup is re-shown after a preempt + priority promotion, so the player's answer bounces with 'another matter has arrived since' — 4 of 24 turns in the flagship, mock and live
findings._corrected: Three surfaces write `world.incoming_proposal_popup`; IGR-F made the DELIVERY write conditional on the dialogue being current (ai_diplomacy.py:2045-2061) and the Aug-30 review fixed the counter-offer sibling (world_state.py:10118-10127). A third producer of the same stale-slot class remains: `DialogueManager.preempt` (dialogue_manager.py:322-346) re-queues the current dialogue behind a player-initiated one (the Assess advisory is mounted with `preempt`, diplomatic_executor.py:774), and when that is dismissed `pop` → `_promote` (dialogue_manager.py:347-352, :779-791) promotes by DIALOGUE_PRIORITY — `incoming_settlement_offer` 2 outranks `incoming_proposal` 3 (:185, :191). The settlement offer becomes current, but the popup slot still holds the proposal payload written when the proposal WAS current, and `_include_popup_passthroughs` (main.py:1594-1643) emits it; the client renders Russia's offer while Britain's settlement offer is active, and the id-bound answer hits the W6-0 stale guard (diplomatic_executor.py:3410-3432).

findings.player_consequence: The Russia armistice popup is on screen; clicking Reject (or Accept) returns 'Sire, another matter has arrived since — this concerns Britain. Your earlier answer was not delivered'; the player must answer Britain's offer, and Russia's proposal is never re-presented in that run — it is '(left standing)' and lapses at end of turn, applying the 6-turn lapse cooldown. The player's decision never reaches the court. Reproduced on 4 of 24 turns of the flagship campaign, identically under the live parser.
findings.evidence: Archived: docs/audits/playtest_digests/audit-flagship-mock/digest.md:127-135 (turn 9: `Talleyrand, assess our situation` → `advisory #20 → dismiss` → `Russia, armistice_losing #17 → reject` → `↳ refused: Sire, another matter has arrived since — this concerns Britain…` → `incoming_settlement_offer #19 → reject_settlement_offer` → `Russia, armistice_losing #17 → (left standing)`); same shape at :226-231 (Prussia #31), :262-267 (Britain #36 vs settlement #39), :338-343 (Prussia #51); audit-flagship-live/digest.md:129-135 identical. Verified by opening: dialogue_manager.py:322-346 (preempt re-queues), :347-352 + :779-791 (pop promotes highest priority), :185/:191 (priorities 2 vs 3); ai_diplomacy.py:2045-2061 (delivery write guarded by `peek() is dialogue` only); diplomatic_executor.py:774 (advisory mounted via preempt), :3410-3432 (stale guard text); main.py:1594 (`_include_popup_passthroughs` pops the PopupQueue slot).
findings.repro: 1805 boot via TestClient: deliver an AI `incoming_proposal` so it is current (slot written); `promote_pending_settlement_offers` pushes an `incoming_settlement_offer` (queued); POST /command 'Talleyrand, assess our situation'; POST /respond_to_diplomatic_dialogue dismiss on the advisory; read the response's `diplomatic_dialogue.dialogue_id` vs `world.dialogue_manager.peek()['dialogue_id']` — they differ; POST reject with the rendered id → `stale_dialogue: True`, message 'another matter has arrived since'. The delivery and counter-offer guards stay as they are.

findings.title: A refused first-step attack leaves a PHANTOM standing order on the marshal (0 AP charged, order lives on)
findings._corrected: `_execute_strategic_command` assigns `marshal.strategic_order = order` at backend/commands/strategic_executor.py:1216 BEFORE executing the first step; when the first hop is enemy-held, `_handle_first_step_blocked` (:2030) runs and its aggressive favourable arm (:2131-2153) auto-attacks and, on a refused/failed executor result, does `return result` (:2153) — the raw refusal dict — without clearing the order it just created (contrast the literal arm at :2064-2081, which clears the order and returns `order_cleared: True`). The loop at :1278 returns that dict as the command's result, so the player sees a refusal (success False, no AP charged) while a MOVE_TO order is silently standing and fires at the next end turn (→ the phantom-battle finding above).

findings.title: AI harsh-peace demands are purse-blind on the bilateral P8 path — 270g against a 17,487g treasury at +54 war score, bypassing the gate-blessed EC-W4 pricing
findings._corrected: EC-W4 'Peace with Teeth' re-priced only the multilateral settlement-offer builder (`_settlement_offer_build_terms`, ai_diplomacy.py:3236-3247 constants, :3379-3389 purse-scaled formula). The bilateral P8 'Aggressive Dominance' arm (ai_diplomacy.py:1550-1554, fires at war_score > 40) still builds its demand as `gold_demand = max(200, int(war_score * 5 * gold_mult))` (ai_diplomacy.py:896), never reading either treasury, and `_reduce_p8_demands` (:914-935) can only lower it further toward a flat 200 floor. Verified by running on tests/fixtures/playtest_saves/fixture_t20_ambient.json: Britain's war score vs France +54, France treasury 17,487, P8 terms `[{'type':'gold_lump','value':270}]`, acceptance score 53, unchanged after `_reduce_p8_demands`; the EC-W4 settlement path on the SAME state prices 6,233 (cap 6,994, war age 19). The fixture also carried `Britain|harsh_peace: 5` in `ai_proposal_cooldowns`, i.e. a harsh_peace had been sent in the ambient run one turn before turn 20 — the arm fires in ordinary play.

findings.player_consequence: A decisively beaten France (coalition leader at +54, Paget/Moore across the homeland in audit-latewar-t20) receives a 'Harsh Peace Treaty' that costs ~1.5% of the treasury; accepting ends the war for pocket change and re-declaration is priced only in DP/relations (WO-D8). The July-17 absurdity the memo fixed ('Britain at +24 extracts 600g of a 61k hoard', ECON_WAR_COUPLING_RESEARCH_2026_07_17.md:28) survives verbatim on the bilateral channel, and GR5 is broken in the other direction too: an AI at +54 never dictates a real indemnity, so the AI's own 'winning' has no economic teeth.
findings.evidence: Verified by opening: backend/game_logic/ai_diplomacy.py:893-897 (harsh_peace builder), :1550-1554 (P8 gate), :914-935 (`_reduce_p8_demands` halving to floor 200), :3236-3247 (`SETTLEMENT_OFFER_TREASURY_FRACTION=0.15`, `MAX_TREASURY_FRACTION=0.40`, `PER_WAR_SCORE=40`), :3379-3389 (purse formula lives only in the settlement builder); docs/audits/ECON_WAR_COUPLING_RESEARCH_2026_07_17.md:28 and :171 ('`_settlement_offer_build_terms` rewritten' — the landing names only that builder). Verified by running (scratch probe_t20c.py on the committed t20 fixture): P8 demand 270 / acceptance 53 / post-reduce 270 vs EC-W4 6,233 on identical state; France treasury 17,487; Britain WE 154, gold 9,425.
findings.repro: cd repo; .venv/Scripts/python.exe -c "import os,json,sys; os.environ.pop('SOVEREIGN_SCENARIO',None); from backend.models.world_state import WorldState; from backend.game_logic import ai_diplomacy as ad; w=WorldState.from_dict(json.load(open('tests/fixtures/playtest_saves/fixture_t20_ambient.json',encoding='utf-8'))['world_state']); ws=ad._get_war_score_for_nation('Britain','France',w); t=ad._build_proposal_terms('Britain','harsh_peace',ws,w,gold_mult=1.0); print(ws, w.gold, t['demands'])"  → 54 17487 [{'type': 'gold_lump', 'value': 270}]
findings.fix_shape: ONE seam: the `harsh_peace` arm of `_build_proposal_terms` (ai_diplomacy.py:893-897). Extract the EC-W4 purse formula (base + war-age + |score|×PER_WAR_SCORE + payer_treasury×FRACTION, capped at payer_treasury×MAX_FRACTION, empty chest → no lump) into one helper that BOTH `_settlement_offer_build_terms` and the P8 arm call with `payer = recipient`; make `_reduce_p8_demands` halve relative to that figure instead of flooring at 200. No new fields; AI-side acceptance already scores the lump.
findings.behaviour_test: tests/test_econ_war_coupling.py: load fixture_t20_ambient, build Britain `harsh_peace` vs France; assert gold_lump ≥ 0.15×France treasury and ≤ 0.40×; assert it equals `_settlement_offer_build_terms` on the same state within the war-age term; negative control: set France treasury 0 → no gold_lump demand; pin that `_reduce_p8_demands` never lowers the lump below 0.15×treasury while acceptance ≥ 20.
findings.already_filed: DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md A4 (:983-985) records the same formula as a 'historical note only' — it documents, not files, the defect; EC-W4 (memo row 4) and BUG_FIXES have no row for the bilateral P8 arm. findings.title: An addressee the roster cannot resolve is silently DROPPED and the attack auto-assigned to whoever is nearest — "the Iron Marshal, attack Mack" / "Berthier, attack Mack" send Soult
findings._corrected: Two gaps in one seam. (a) ADDRESS_TOKEN_RE (llm_client.py:71-72, verified by opening) captures a SINGLE word before the comma, so multi-word addressees ("the Iron Marshal,", "Prince of Moskowa,", "the cavalry,") never reach `_unresolved_address_token` (:291-320) or CR-2's did-you-mean. (b) A single-word addressee that merely RESEMBLES a region is skipped rather than refused: in the parser word-scan below parser.py:1074 (`was_addressed`), a marshal 'error' falls to `target_check` against regions+enemies and the word is skipped as 'might be a target' — verified by running FuzzyMatcher: 'Berthier' vs marshals = error, vs targets = suggest 'Bern' at 75. Either way marshal=None, `_classify_command` (parser.py:1915-1945) returns `auto_assign_attack`, and `resolve_auto_attack`'s auto_assign arm (combat_executor.py:8748ff) names the nearest marshal instantly (blessed by the CR-6 gate for a BARE 'attack Mack', but here the player DID name someone).

(a) ADDRESS_TOKEN_RE (llm_client.py:71-72, verified by opening) captures a SINGLE word before the comma, so multi-word addressees ("the Iron Marshal,", "Prince of Moskowa,", "the cavalry,") never reach `_unresolved_address_token` (:291-320) or CR-2's did-you-mean. (b) A single-word addressee that merely RESEMBLES a region is skipped rather than refused: in the parser word-scan below parser.py:1074 (`was_addressed`), a marshal 'error' falls to `target_check` against regions+enemies and the word is skipped as 'might be a target' — verified by running FuzzyMatcher: 'Berthier' vs marshals = error, vs targets = suggest 'Bern' at 75. Either way marshal=None, `_classify_command` (parser.py:1915-1945) returns `auto_assign_attack`, and `resolve_auto_attack`'s auto_assign arm (combat_executor.py:8748ff) names the nearest marshal instantly (blessed by the CR-6 gate for a BARE 'attack Mack', but here the player DID name someone).
findings.player_consequence: Verified by running: `the Iron Marshal, attack Mack`, `Iron Marshal, attack Mack`, `Berthier, attack Mack`, `Prince of Moskowa, attack Mack`, `the cavalry, attack Mack`, `the reserve, attack Mack` → all "MUSTER — Soult (30,000; 101,499 if all march) vs Mack" + a battle_report (Mack strength 0 afterwards). The player asked for Davout (Iron Marshal) / Ney (Prince of the Moskowa) / the cavalry (Murat) and the literal-personality Soult marched; the only disclosure is the marshal's name inside the MUSTER line. `the Guard, attack Mack` → the hold keyword 'guard' (llm_client.py:1485) makes it a HOLD/auto_assign parse with target 'generic' and the player sees the raw string "Error: No target or world state" (combat_executor.py:8647-8649). Contrast `Grouchy, attack Mack` → "There is no Marshal 'Grouchy' in the order of battle, Sire. Whom did you intend?" — the guard exists and these shapes bypass it.
findings.evidence: verified by opening backend/ai/llm_client.py:71-72, :80-97 (ADDRESS_NON_NAME_WORDS includes cavalry/guard), :291-320; backend/commands/parser.py:1074-1176 word-scan, :1915-1945 `_classify_command`; backend/commands/combat_executor.py:8636-8649 and :8748-8797; verified by running the /command probes and a FuzzyMatcher probe.
findings.repro: POST /command {"command":"the Iron Marshal, attack Mack"} or {"command":"Berthier, attack Mack"} on the 1805 boot → MUSTER led by Soult + battle_report; {"command":"the Guard, attack Mack"} → message "Error: No target or world state".
findings.fix_shape: ONE seam — the addressee extraction: make ADDRESS_TOKEN_RE capture the whole pre-comma phrase (`^\s*(?:the\s+)?([A-Za-z][\w'’ -]{1,40}?)\s*,`) so `_leading_addressed_token` sees multi-word addressees, and in the parser word-scan treat `was_addressed and marshal_result['action']=='error'` as `marshal_not_found` regardless of `target_check` (a comma-addressed token is never a target). Then an unbound addressed attack raises the CR-2 'Whom did you intend?' question and never reaches `_classify_command`'s auto-assign.
findings.behaviour_test: each of the six phrasings → success False, kind marshal_not_found/marshal_suggest, no battle_report, Soult still at Lorraine at 30,000; bare `attack Mack` keeps the CR-6 instant pick (test_cr6_bare_attack_gating stays green); `the Guard, attack Mack` never returns a string starting with 'Error:'.
findings.already_filed: CR-2 (f) silent-marshal-drop (COMMAND_ROBUSTNESS_SPEC.md:29) covers single-token addressees on META actions only

findings.title: An enemy garrison assault on French soil is invisible on every surface unless the assaulter's own province is FULL
findings._corrected: `_resolve_garrison_combat` (backend/commands/combat_executor.py:2857-3157) calls `world.log_event` zero times (verified by awk over the whole function) and returns only a private `events: [{"type": "garrison_assault", ...}]` row (:3148) or `garrison_destroyed`/`occupation_started` (:3051-3061). The enemy-phase fog filter `_filter_enemy_phase_by_visibility` (backend/main.py) treats a row as involving the player only for `battle`/`bombardment` events (:1749), an `ai_action.target` that is a player MARSHAL, or an event stamped `captured_from == player` (:1798) — a `garrison_assault` on a player-controlled region satisfies none, so the row falls to the region check and is suppressed when the assaulter stands on a PARTIAL province (the ordinary P4.25 case: `_find_garrison_attack` picks an ADJACENT garrison, enemy_ai.py:1981-1989). Verified by running: Mack at Swabia (vis `partial`) assaulting the Rhineland garrison on the 1805 boot board → `survives filter: 0`. Even when a row survives, `enemy_phase_dialog.gd::_format_action` (:121, events loop :248-272) has arms only for `battle`/`bombardment`/`conquest`, so the line renders as a bare `- Mack attacks Milan`. `garrison_assault` is in neither `CAMPAIGN_LOG_TYPES` (backend/campaign_log.py:94, grep = 0 hits) nor the gazette's `_WAR_TYPES` (backend/game_logic/gazette.py:32-36), no notification type exists (backend/notifications.py grep 'garrison' = 0), and the dispatch has no class for it.

findings.title: Attacking a marshal France holds prisoner answers 'Unknown target' one turn after the dispatch called him 'our prisoner' — and the parser comment claiming PC15-4 covers it is false
findings._corrected: Archived digest: T2 'Marshal Kienmayer of Austria is taken at Swabia — he is our prisoner' (audit-tutorial/digest.md:23), T3 `Ney, attack Kienmayer` -> 'Unknown target: Kienmayer' (:26). Mechanism verified by opening: `_fuzzy_match_enemy` (executor.py:719-748) looks the name up through `get_enemy_by_name_for_nation` which requires strength > 0 (world_state.py:3750-3755), so a prisoner (strength 0 at the captor's capital) is 'not found'; the honest 'Enemy X not found. Available: …' error is then DISCARDED by combat_executor.py:4596-4601 (returned only when it carries 'Did you mean' or `refused_marshal_correction`), the region fuzzy finds nothing, and the bare fall-through at combat_executor.py:5095-5098 prints 'Unknown target'. parser.py:1380-1381 asserts 'a PRISONER is not a target … PC15-4 already refuses him by name', but `_addressed_lost_marshal_refusal` (main.py:894-925) reads only the LEADING addressed token against the PLAYER's roster and tombs — an enemy prisoner as a TARGET is never seen. Three surfaces give three different answers to one question.

findings.player_consequence: The player copies the game's own sentence and is told the man does not exist. `attack Kienmayer` (bare) says 'Kienmayer has already been destroyed!' of a living prisoner; `Ney, pursue Kienmayer` is ACCEPTED, charges 2 AP, prints '(at unknown)' and physically marches Ney to Swabia toward a man sitting in Paris. In the School of War this is the suggest chip of step VII when the player took the card's first-listed answer (trust).
findings.evidence: Verified by running (scratch script over TestClient, INK_IRON_SAVE_DIR sandboxed): /new_game {scenario: tutorial}; set Kienmayer strength=0, captured_by='France', location='Paris'; then `Ney, attack Kienmayer` -> False 'Unknown target: Kienmayer'; `attack Kienmayer` -> False 'Kienmayer has already been destroyed!'; `Ney, pursue Kienmayer` -> True 'Ney pursues Kienmayer (at unknown). Moves to Swabia.' Verified by opening: executor.py:719-748, world_state.py:3737-3755, combat_executor.py:4563-4601 and :5095-5098, parser.py:1370-1385, main.py:894-925, strategic_executor.py:1509-1517 (`_pursue_known_location` -> 'unknown').
findings.repro: Boot any world, capture an enemy marshal (or set `m.strength=0; m.captured_by='France'; m.location='Paris'`), POST /command 'Ney, attack <name>', 'attack <name>', 'Ney, pursue <name>'.

findings.title: Infantry forms square (1 AP) and then attacks — breaking the square — in the same enemy phase, every phase
findings._corrected: P2.5 (enemy_ai.py:1795-1840) forms square whenever enemy cavalry is adjacent, no artillery is adjacent and the cooldown/latch permit (condition at :1835), and it is evaluated BEFORE P4; the same marshal is then re-selected, P4 finds his attack, and the attack breaks the square via `_auto_break_square` (tactical_executor.py:461-485), which sets no `ai_square_cooldown`, so the square is formed again next phase. `form_square` costs 1 AP (world_state.py:942). PT-F6's latch stops the form/break/RE-form thrash within a phase and deliberately leaves 'attack breaks legal', which is exactly the surviving waste: one paid action per infantry marshal per phase on a formation he discards seconds later.

findings.title: Popup queue and dialogue stack disagree after any re-promotion: the envoy popup the game shows is refused as stale when clicked
findings._corrected: PopupQueue.PRIORITY_ORDER delivers `incoming_proposal_popup` ABOVE `incoming_settlement_offer_popup` (backend/models/cooldown_manager.py:158-159, verified by opening) while DialogueManager.DIALOGUE_PRIORITY ranks a settlement offer (2) ABOVE a proposal (3) (backend/models/dialogue_manager.py:185,191) and `_promote()` re-sorts the queue by that priority on every pop (dialogue_manager.py:779-793). A proposal arrives first (current, its popup payload written at ai_diplomacy.py:2058-2064 because `peek() is dialogue`), a settlement offer arrives second (queued, its popup pushed at turn_manager.py:621-623). Any preempt-then-pop in between — a Talleyrand `advisory` (assess), a CR-2 clarification, a delegation ASK, a hard stop — promotes the SETTLEMENT to active, but `_include_popup_passthroughs` (main.py:1594-1699) pops the PROPOSAL payload (main.py:1620) without checking it against the active dialogue's id. The W6-0 guard (diplomatic_executor.py:3404-3432) then correctly refuses the click as stale. Verified by running (scratch repro_desync.py): after arrivals active=incoming_proposal#1; after advisory preempt+pop active=incoming_settlement_offer#2 while the delivered popup is `{'from_nation': 'Russia', 'dialogue_id': 1}`; answering it → `success False, stale_dialogue True, 'Sire, another matter has arrived since — this concerns Britain.'` The safety valve at main.py:1666-1685 only fires when NO winner was popped, so it cannot correct this.

Measured 4 times in the 24-turn flagship: audit-flagship-mock/digest.md:129-135 (turn 9, Russia armistice #17 vs settlement #19), :226-231 (t14, Prussia #31 vs #33), :262-267 (t16, Britain #36 vs #39), :338-343 (t21, Prussia #51 vs #53) — every one the verbatim line `↳ refused: Sire, another matter has arrived since — this concerns Britain. findings.evidence: cooldown_manager.py:145-163 PRIORITY_ORDER (proposal :158 above settlement :159); dialogue_manager.py:175-194 DIALOGUE_PRIORITY (settlement 2, proposal 3), :322-345 preempt, :347-353 pop→_promote, :779-793 _promote re-sort; main.py:1620 pop_highest delivered unconditionally, :1666-1685 safety valve gated on `winner_attr is None`; ai_diplomacy.py:2043-2064 popup written only while current; turn_manager.py:619-623 settlement popup push; diplomatic_executor.py:3404-3432 stale refusal. Digest lines cited above. Runtime repro output quoted in summary.
findings.repro: python snippet: TestClient(/new_game); dm=world.dialogue_manager; dm.push(incoming_proposal dict for Russia with popup_payload); world.incoming_proposal_popup=copy(payload); dm.push(incoming_settlement_offer dict for Britain); world._popup_queue.push('incoming_settlement_offer_popup', payload); dm.preempt({'type':'advisory',...}); dm.pop(); resp={}; main._include_popup_passthroughs(resp, world) → resp['incoming_proposal']['dialogue_id']==1 while dm.peek()['dialogue_id']==2; executor.handle_diplomatic_dialogue_response('reject', game_state, dialogue_id=1) → stale_dialogue=True. In-game: with a Prussian/Russian proposal and a Britain settlement offer both pending on turn start, type 'Talleyrand, assess our situation', dismiss, then answer the envoy popup that appears.
findings.fix_shape: ONE seam, `_include_popup_passthroughs` (backend/main.py:1620-1640): after `pop_highest`, if `winner_key in ('incoming_proposal','incoming_settlement_offer')` and `winner_value.get('dialogue_id')` differs from `world.dialogue_manager.peek().get('dialogue_id')`, push the winner back (`world._popup_queue.push(winner_attr, winner_value)`) and instead deliver the popup derived from the ACTIVE dialogue — `_build_pending_envoy_popup_from_dialogue` (main.py:4374) for proposals, `build_incoming_settlement_offer_popup` (the /pending_envoy arm, main.py:4460-4467) for settlement offers. Do not touch DialogueManager priorities or the W6-0 guard.
findings.behaviour_test: tests/test_response_pipeline.py: push proposal A then settlement B on a boot world (popups queued as the producers do), `dm.preempt(advisory)`, `dm.pop()`, then `_include_popup_passthroughs(resp, world)`; assert the ONE non-None envoy key carries `dialogue_id == dm.peek()['dialogue_id']`, and `handle_diplomatic_dialogue_response('reject', gs, dialogue_id=<delivered id>)` returns success with no `stale_dialogue`. Negative control: without the fix the assertion fails exactly as the repro shows.
findings.already_filed: BUG-CA-7 (FIXED — landed the W6-0 identity guard that now refuses these clicks); IGR-F note at ai_diplomacy.py:2043-2056 fixed the sibling last-write-wins variant. The re-promotion desync between the two queues is NOT filed in BUG_FIXES.md or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md (grepped 'another matter has arrived', 'PRIORITY_ORDER', 'popup queue').

findings.title: Shipped build: when the server is down the menu and the in-game connection failure tell the stranger to run a Python command that does not exist in the zip
findings._corrected: main_menu.gd:527 status line: 'The war office does not answer — start the backend:  .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m backend.main'; main.gd:745: 'Start the Python server: python -m backend.main'; main_menu.gd:346 version line 'Ink & Iron — development build'. No script anywhere branches on OS.has_feature('editor'/'template') (grep across main_menu.gd/main.gd/utils.gd/settings_panel.gd/api_client.gd: zero hits), so the exported client shows the developer command verbatim. Keep the dev string so test_main_menu_and_ux_pass.py:129 holds, and add the template arm to the same pin.

findings.title: The /command question-bearing early returns still DRAIN the PopupQueue into a response the client renders only one route of — deferred one-shot popups are destroyed, petitions delayed, and the question itself can go unrendered
findings._corrected: `_build_result_response(result, world)` drains by default (main.py:462-500) and is used unchanged on the /command early returns for a tactical objection (main.py:3028), strategic objection (:3032), clarification (:3044), glorious charge (:3051), strategic interrupt (:3059), diplomatic dialogue (:3075), the typed interrupt route (:2263) and /marshal_petition_response (:3203). Only the capture arm was converted to `drain_popups=False` (:3068, IGR-X7). On the client, `_on_command_result` returns at the FIRST matching route: pre-HUD objection/glorious-charge routes at main.gd:2492 (`_show_objection_dialog` main.gd:3945 reads no popup key — grep verified), post-HUD table at main.gd:1924-1937 with `marshal_petition` idx 2 ahead of `proposal_confirm` idx 6, `clarification` idx 7, `interrupt` idx 8, returning at main.gd:2514. Verified by running: (a) repro_objdrain.py — a queued `diplomatic_sabotage_popup` was delivered INSIDE Bernadotte's objection response (`state awaiting_player_choice`, `diplomatic_sabotage` non-None), the queue was empty afterwards and the key was None on `/respond_to_objection` and on the next `/command`; (b) repro_stack2.py — 'propose peace with Austria' with a queued petition returned BOTH `marshal_petition` and `diplomatic_dialogue proposal_confirm#1`; 'move to Brittany' returned BOTH `marshal_petition` and `state awaiting_clarification` ('Which marshal shall march to Brittany, Sire?') with `command_clarification` left active. findings.title: The WIN-D3 road-home order loses its first turn, so a corps that marches home is warned 'no nearer home — 2 turns of safe passage left' every turn, the morning after the beat promised 7
findings._corrected: `_issue_road_home_orders` stamps the free MOVE_TO with `issued_turn=int(world.current_turn)` (withdrawal.py:691) but executes NO first step, while `process_strategic_orders` skips any order whose `issued_turn == world.current_turn` because 'first step already executed by executor.py' (strategic.py:260-264) — true for the executor's issuance (strategic_executor.py:1300+), false for the treaty's. `advance_turn` increments the turn (world_state.py:9388) and then ticks the corridor (:9789): expiry = t + dist + slack(3), so after the lost turn surplus = 2 = `EVACUATION_WARNING_MARGIN` (withdrawal.py:120, :797-800) and, because a steadily marching corps keeps its surplus constant by design, he is warned EVERY turn until home. They have safe passage for 7 turns while they march.'; same-turn strategic pass reports only 'Davout is marching to Franche-Comte (5 turn(s) remaining)' (skipped); tick turn 2 (still at Vienna): 'Davout is no nearer home — 4 march(es) still to go from Vienna, and 2 turn(s) of safe passage left before his corps is interned.'; tick turn 3 after marching to Bohemia: 'Davout is no nearer home — 3 march(es) still to go … 2 turn(s) … left'. findings.title: The combat_stalemate popup asks 'Continue move to?' and its 'Continue as Ordered' button cancels the order
findings._corrected: strategic.py:2961 builds the stalemate-interrupt message via `order.command_type.replace('_',' ').lower()` ("Continue move to?"), offering `["continue_order","hold_position","cancel_order"]` (options list at 2950/2962). `_respond_combat_stalemate` (strategic.py:812-865) makes ALL THREE options null `marshal.strategic_order` and end the march — `continue_order`/`attack_again` (817-826) does so at zero trust cost with the message "…cannot break through. Orders cancelled — awaiting new instructions," while `hold_position`/`cancel_order` do the same at −3 trust. The client (interrupt_popup.gd:27-30) labels `continue_order` "Continue as Ordered," so the one free-looking button is the one that silently cancels the standing order — confirmed independently by audit-naval/digest.md Turns 11→14 (Turn 11 answers `continue_order`; Turn 14's identical "march to London" command creates a fresh order rather than reporting "already carrying out that order," proving the prior march had been cancelled). This is not required for loop-prevention: `order.combat_attempts` + `_should_auto_attack` (strategic.py:2966-2982, six call sites, every personality) already gate re-attack on the same enemy independent of whether the order object survives, and would route a next-turn contact into the existing "still blocks the path... Previous assault was inconclusive" ask (strategic.py:2778-2780) if the order were kept standing. Fix: in `_respond_combat_stalemate`, `continue_order` should keep `marshal.strategic_order` set (only `cancel_order`/`hold_position` null it), and the popup message should build via the already-used `_strategic_command_flavor(order.command_type)` helper (strategic.py:28-34, which returns "his march" for MOVE_TO, matching a message "Continue his march?") instead of the raw snake_case replace.

Orders cancelled — awaiting new instructions.' The client renders `continue_order` as 'Continue as Ordered' (godot-client/project-sovereign/scripts/interrupt_popup.gd:30). findings.title: The enemy AI is pinned on a doomed stub: P4 has no target-worth floor and the aggressive pick maximises the ratio, so three Austrian corps spent four turns killing 58 men while Paris stood empty
findings._corrected: P4 admits any enemy with `enemy.strength > 0` (enemy_ai.py:2739) and the aggressive pick is `max(attackable, key=ratio)` (:3017-3021); P0 forces an attack on the weakest co-located enemy whenever the ratio clears the threshold (:1615, :1674). A 702-man or 58-man corps therefore has the best ratio on the board and is attacked first, every action, by every co-located corps. findings.title: A war purpose set against Austria ticks into the coalition war score but is invisible on the panel — the row resolves the objective through the LEADER pair only
findings._corrected: `calculate_side_war_score` sums the `ticking` component across EVERY opponent pair of a coalition war (`diplomacy.py:3259-3281`), but `build_active_wars` resolves the row's `objective`/`enemy_objective` through `diplo_key = _make_diplo_key(france, opponent)` where `opponent` is the coalition leader (`war_status.py:56`, `:157`). Verified by running: `set war purpose` vs Austria → `war_objectives == {'Austria|France': ['France']}` and the row still shows `objective None`; vs Britain (the leader) → `objective {'type':'conquest','target_regions':['London'],...}` renders. So the only renderable French purpose in the 1805 coalition targets London — the province the Wooden Wall (A5) makes unreachable — while the historically correct aim (Vienna) is computed and hidden.

The WO-17 direction term (withdrawal.py:141-192, keyed on `is_stranded_at`) admits any step by a corps stranded where it stands, so the 'rush' can go DEEPER into the partner's territory. The corridor tick `process_evacuation_grants` (:719-830) warns and interns but never calls `_issue_road_home_orders` again. The AI's corps are immune (P1.2 recomputes `next_step_home` each turn, :624-651) — the asymmetry is against the player.
findings.player_consequence: Verified by running (probe_strategic3.py R): Lannes stranded at Volhynia, peace with Russia → road-home MOVE_TO Franche-Comte (7 marches, grant expiry 11). A Prussia-vs-Russia battle at Estonia (both at PEACE with France): 'Lannes hears cannon fire! Abandoning orders — rushing to Estonia! Lannes moves from Volhynia to White Russia (180 lost to march)'; order None; +1 'Lannes is no nearer home — 8 march(es) still to go from White Russia, and 1 turn(s) of safe passage left'; +2 '0 turn(s)'; +3 'Lannes's corps failed to quit Russia soil before its safe passage expired. It has been disarmed and interned.' A player who misses one line in the strategic report loses the corps that won the war — the exact outcome WIN-D3 was built to prevent.
findings.evidence: Verified by opening strategic.py:2247-2307 (no road-home check; order nulled at :2307), withdrawal.py:141-192, :624-651, :654-704, :719-830 (no re-issue), :844-890 (warn/intern). Verified by running probe R — output quoted above verbatim.
findings.repro: Boot 1805; set `w.regions['Volhynia'].controller='France'`; park other French marshals at Paris and Russians at their capital; `lannes.location='Volhynia'`; `set_diplomatic_state(w,'France','Russia','WAR')` then `'PEACE'` (issues the road-home order); `lannes.strategic_order.issued_turn -= 1`; `w.record_battle('Estonia','Hohenlohe','Kutuzov','victory')`; `process_strategic_orders` → order None, Lannes at White Russia; then `W.process_evacuation_grants(w)` per turn → interned at +3.
findings.fix_shape: ONE seam: in `_check_interrupts` (strategic.py:2262, beside the literal exemption) `if is_road_home_order(marshal.strategic_order): return None` — the treaty's road is literal by nature. (Belt: have `process_evacuation_grants` re-issue via `_issue_road_home_orders` for an order-less stranded PLAYER corps, so a player-cancelled road is offered again rather than silently lapsing.)
findings.behaviour_test: tests: stranded aggressive player marshal with the road-home order + a third-party battle within 2 → after `process_strategic_orders` the order still stands (`is_road_home_order`), the marshal moved one province HOMEWARD, no `cannon_fire` report; corridor tick over `expiry` turns produces no `evacuation_lapsing`/`marshal_interned` event.
findings.already_filed: WIN-D3 (built, DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md:360) and WO-17 (FIXED) own the corridor; neither covers the interrupt interaction. Unfiled.

findings.title: 'Even the favorable ground could not save Massena' at 1 vs 58 casualties: Berthier's terrain verdict has no scale gate
findings._corrected: `_pick_observation` selects `lost_despite_terrain`/`lost_terrain_disadvantage` purely on `we_lost and terrain-bonus modifier >= 15` (backend/game_logic/battle_report.py:832-838, banks at :333-342) with no floor on battle size — reproduced directly: a 1-vs-58-casualty exchange with a defender terrain-bonus modifier of 20 returns 'Even the favorable ground could not save Massena, Sire. Archduke Charles overcame the terrain.', matching digest line 125 verbatim. The same sub-1000-casualty engagements already fall below the war-score floor (diplomacy.py:9418-9420, `total_casualties < 1000`) and add 0 war exhaustion per side (coalition.py:1436-1437, `casualties // 1000` — note: statement is at line 1436, not 1433 as originally cited; the `def` starts at 1430), so the engine already treats them as sub-battle skirmishes while the narrator gives them the same grave "grim day, Sire" terrain verdict as a real battle. Fix seam confirmed correct: gate in `_pick_observation` before the loss ladder (before line 815, priority 2) using the same >=1000-total-casualty floor already computed from `attacker_casualties`/`defender_casualties` in scope — this is the single call site both player- and AI-initiated battles pass through (GR5-clean), duplicates no existing rule (no scale gate exists anywhere else in this file), and breaks no pinned test (existing `_pick_observation` tests use casualties of 5,000-25,000, well above the proposed floor). Not a duplicate of any filed row — WO-12/WO-15/WO-16 all concern different files/mechanisms (world_state.py mislabels, dispatch.py's `own_mauled` headline predicate), none touch battle_report.py's observation-bank selection.
findings.summary: `_pick_observation` selects `lost_despite_terrain` purely on `we_lost and terrain bonus >= 15` (battle_report.py:836-838) and the bank (:338-342) narrates hills taken and positions overrun regardless of the action's size. Applied to a 58-man remnant it produces the digest's 'Even the favorable ground could not save Massena, Sire. Archduke Charles overcame the terrain' (audit-latewar-t20/digest.md line 125) and, for a 0-vs-163 exchange, 'The hills were ours, but Archduke John took them' (line 113). The same skirmishes already fall below the war-score floor (diplomacy.py:9418-9420, total casualties < 1,000) and add 0 war exhaustion (coalition.py:1433-1436), so the engine knows they are not battles; the narrator does not.
findings.player_consequence: Eleven identically grave 'grim day, Sire' verdicts for a corps that has already ceased to matter, drowning the real headline (the enemy massing on the capital road) and teaching the player to skim Berthier.

findings.title: 'build ships' blames green crews for a readiness fall that is 5/6 blockade rot — the player concludes building makes the fleet worse
findings._corrected: `lay_down_ship` folds one 40-readiness hull into the fleet (naval.py:1941): at 46 sail that costs ~1 point. `_readiness_tick` (naval.py:1573) then rots a BLOCKADED fleet −5/turn. The build result (naval_executor.py:60-66) prints the post-fold readiness with the clause '(new crews come aboard green at 40; only sea-time makes a navy)' and never names the blockade, so four consecutive keels read 69→63→58→53 as if each keel cost five points.
findings.summary: `lay_down_ship` folds one 40-readiness hull into the fleet (naval.py:1941): at 46 sail that costs ~1 point. `_readiness_tick` (naval.py:1573) then rots a BLOCKADED fleet −5/turn. The build result (naval_executor.py:60-66) prints the post-fold readiness with the clause '(new crews come aboard green at 40; only sea-time makes a navy)' and never names the blockade, so four consecutive keels read 69→63→58→53 as if each keel cost five points.
findings.player_consequence: The archived run's player spent 1,600g on four keels and watched readiness fall 16 points 'because of green crews'; effective strength went 31.5→26. Being blockaded by Britain — the actual cause, stated only on the Admiralty tab and inside the blockade order's own message — is invisible at the one surface where the number moves. The user's own question ('is building ships making the fleet worse?') has the answer 'no, the blockade is' and the game says the opposite.
findings.evidence: Verified by running: `lay_down_ship` at 46@64 → 47@63 (−1); `_readiness_tick` from 69 while blockaded → 64. The digest's sequence reproduces exactly only as fold(−1)+rot(−5) per turn: 70→69→64→63→58→58→53→50. Archived digest audit-naval turns 1-4: 'readiness 69 … 63 … 58 … 53 (new crews come aboard green at 40; only sea-time makes a navy)'. Verified by opening naval_executor.py:57-68, naval.py:1926-1946, :1560-1580.
findings.repro: In-game on the 1805 boot: 'build ships' on four consecutive turns; compare the quoted readiness against `naval.lay_down_ship`'s pre/post and `blockade_forecast(w,'France')['self_blockaded_by']` (Britain).
findings.fix_shape: Have `lay_down_ship` return `readiness_before`; the build message quotes the fold delta and, when `blockade_forecast(world, actor)['self_blockaded_by']` is set, adds the rot clause from the same single source the blockade order uses ('a green crew costs 1 point; the Royal Navy's blockade rots her 5 a turn — that is the number to fix').
findings.behaviour_test: test_build_message_attributes_readiness_honestly: blockaded boot → message names the blockader and quotes delta == before − after (1); after Britain flips to guard (staged camp) → no rot clause; the quoted delta never exceeds the fold. Mutation: drop the blockader clause → red.
findings.already_filed: WO-D3 (carried) records the OPPOSITE reading — 'building ships LOWERS readiness (69 → 50 over ten keels) and the message says why'; measured here, the message names the smaller of two causes.

findings.title: A MOVE_TO whose last leg is a SHUT sea link is accepted with a route and no warning
findings._corrected: CONFIRMED as filed, with one refinement to the fix_shape: order-issuance route-building in `_execute_strategic_command` (backend/commands/strategic_executor.py:1507, message built from `route_str = \" -> \".join([marshal.location] + order.path)`) never consults naval state — `world.find_weighted_path`/`find_path` (backend/models/world_state.py:4943-5070) walk `adjacent_regions` unconditionally and the only passability gate they call, `_region_passable_for` (world_state.py:4919), is diplomatic-only. The per-turn step correctly gates via `movement_executor._execute_move`'s crossing check (movement_executor.py:153-170), so the SHUT verdict only surfaces after the marshal physically halts at the coast, turns later, not at order acceptance — reproduced verbatim in docs/audits/playtest_digests/audit-naval/digest.md:80. Fix: at the strategic_executor.py:1507 seam, walk `order.path` pairwise (`is_sea_link`/`crossing_check` from backend/game_logic/naval.py) and append a warning or refuse when a leg is SHUT — this mirrors the existing two-leg crossing check already shipped at movement_executor.py:490-510, so it is the correct existing idiom, not a new parallel rule. Drop the finding's secondary suggestion of reusing `move_refusal_probe` as an alternative refusal path — that helper (movement_executor.py:125) only probes the immediate next hop and would not catch a SHUT leg buried later in a multi-hop route like this repro's fourth leg.
findings.summary: Order issuance builds the route with `find_weighted_path` (sea links are walkable edges) and prints "Ney begins march to London. Route: Flanders -> Westphalia -> Artois -> Normandy -> London" without consulting `naval.crossing_check`; strategic_executor.py contains no crossing reference at all. The gate first bites four turns later at the per-turn step (and then as FA-19's false stalemate).
findings.player_consequence: 2 AP and four turns marching a 23k corps to a coast it cannot leave; the Crossings board said 'London–Normandy: SHUT' on the same turn the order was accepted.
findings.evidence: Verified by opening docs/audits/playtest_digests/audit-naval/digest.md:80 (the route line, turn 6) and backend/commands/strategic_executor.py:1500-1507 (route string built from `order.path`, message at :1507; grep of strategic_executor.py for 'crossing'/'blocked_naval' returns nothing). Verified by running: the t4 and t7 snapshots both carry `fleets['__naval__']['verdicts']['London|Normandy'] == 'shut'`; t10 shows Ney at Artois with path ['Normandy','London'], t13 shows Ney at Normandy with no order — he never crossed.

findings.title: Real-world exonyms auto-correct into the wrong province and the strategic march never says so — "Ney, march to Mainz" marches six provinces WEST to Maine; "march to Bayern" heads for Bern

findings.title: The fleet-action loss line sums the pooled allies' losses under the loser's name ('loses 49 sail' with 45 in commission)
findings._corrected: CONFIRMED as filed, line numbers exact (naval.py:1516 `resolve_diversion`, naval.py:1264 `_log_fleet_action`'s `loser_ships_lost`, naval_executor.py:370 expedition-intercept message). Live-reproduced: forcing a diversion loss on the 1805 boot (France allied to Spain, Holland its vassal, all three at war with Britain) drove France's own fleet 45→20 (25 ships) while the game's own message read "loses 49 sail" — the sum of France's 25 + Spain's 17 + Holland's 7. findings.title: The letter-book re-asks the identical declined pact every 4 turns forever — `friendly_gift` and `open_borders` are two cooldown keys for one displayed 'Open Borders Agreement'
findings._corrected: For a court at relation<0, `_hegemony_ask_candidates` (ai_diplomacy.py:1005-1055) orders `["friendly_gift","open_borders"]`; `friendly_gift`'s terms (built at :802-819) set `terms["type"]="open_borders"` (or `"non_aggression"` at relation>=0), so it IS the same letter as the literal ask of that base state — `envoy_digest.py:101-112` titles the letter-book row from `terms["type"]`, not the internal label. `_cooldown_keys` (ai_diplomacy.py:305-323) keys the anti-monotony cooldown on the raw `proposal_type` string, so `friendly_gift` and its base (`open_borders` or `non_aggression`) never share a cooldown slot even though the player reads one pact — confirmed live by an independent probe (Ottoman alternates friendly_gift/open_borders every ~3-4 turns at relation -20; Hesse alternates non_aggression/friendly_gift at relation 0, explaining N30's own cited 'Hesse re-raised one pact 5x' example, which N30 left unexplained). Archived evidence checks out exactly (Ottoman x6/Portugal x6/Denmark x6/Saxony x6/Hesse x5/PapalStates x5 in audit-flagship-mock, hand-verified), EXCEPT the '8 of 9 arms' count: audit-latewar-t20 also has zero LETTER rows (not just tutorial), so it's 7 of 9 arms showing letters, and only 6 of those show the repeat-decline cadence (audit-propose runs under accept policy so shows only the first-ask title collision). Fix seam and shape are correct and does not reintroduce the 'documented trap' the codebase deliberately avoids (that trap is about keying cooldowns on an arbitrarily-rewritten terms['type'] for ANY proposal type such as design_purchase; the proposed fix is a narrow, hand-authored 2-way mapping scoped to exactly proposal_type=='friendly_gift', whose base is always one of the four canonical ladder states) — already_filed correctly names N30 as the same root cause/seam but under-specified; this finding should be merged into N30's row with the added mechanism, not discarded.
findings.summary: For a court at relation < 0 `_hegemony_ask_candidates` orders `['friendly_gift','open_borders']` (ai_diplomacy.py:1027-1030); a friendly_gift 'softens' the open_borders ask (its base is open_borders, :1039-1041) and PT-D3 titles the letter-book row from the terms it carries (envoy_digest.py:101-112), so both keys render 'Open Borders Agreement'. The TYPE rejection cooldown (`TYPE_REJECTION_COOLDOWN=6`, ai_diplomacy.py:50) is keyed on the internal P-rule label (`_cooldown_keys`, :322-325), so declining the friendly_gift leaves the `open_borders` key free once the 3-turn NATION cooldown (:46) expires. Verified by running: turn-2 cooldowns `Ottoman|friendly_gift: 6, Ottoman|nation: 3`; turn 6 `Ottoman|open_borders: 6` (friendly_gift still at 2) — a different key, the same letter. Result: the same seven courts re-send the same declined ask on a 4-turn cycle (turn 2 → 6 → 10 → 14 → 18 → 22) for the whole campaign.
findings.player_consequence: Every fourth turn the letter-book carries the exact ask the player already declined: flagship 24 turns = Ottoman ×6, Portugal ×6, Denmark ×6, Saxony ×6, Hesse ×5, PapalStates ×5 (Denmark alternating NAP/Open Borders). Declining has no memory; the surface IGR-F built to make minor-court mail tolerable reads as spam, and 'the court noted your refusal' is a lie the cadence tells against itself.

refuters.reason: Independently reproduced beyond what the original finding did. Read `_hegemony_ask_candidates` (ai_diplomacy.py:1005-1055) and `_build_proposal_terms`'s friendly_gift branch (:802-819): for relation<0 the candidate order is `["friendly_gift","open_borders"]`, and `friendly_gift`'s `terms["type"]` is set to `"open_borders"` (relation<0) or `"non_aggression"` (relation>=0) — so it is mechanically the same letter as the literal ask of that base state. `envoy_digest.py:101-112` confirms the row title is `payload["proposal_type_display"]`, which `mailbox_payloads` builds from `terms["type"]`, not the P-rule label — so both render the identical title. `_cooldown_keys` (ai_diplomacy.py:305-323, not 305-325 — the closing `)` is at 323) builds `type_key = f"{nation}|{proposal_type}"` off the RAW label, so `friendly_gift` and `open_borders` (or `friendly_gift` and `non_aggression`) never share a cooldown slot even though the player sees one pact. `apply_rejection_cooldowns` (ai_diplomacy.py:383-401, called from `_handle_reject_ai_proposal` at diplomatic_executor.py:6487/6501, matching the citation) keys off the same raw `proposal_type`. I then ran an independent scratch probe (`WorldState.from_scenario` on the real 1805 map, calling `process_diplomatic_phase` turn-by-turn with `apply_rejection_cooldowns` after each hit) and reproduced the exact alternation live: Ottoman `friendly_gift`(terms=open_borders) → `open_borders` → `friendly_gift` → `open_borders`, at relation −20; Hesse `non_aggression` → `friendly_gift`(terms=non_aggression) → `non_aggression` → `friendly_gift`, at relation 0 — which is also the precise, previously-unexplained mechanism behind N30's own cited example ('Hesse re-raised one pact 5×'). I spot-checked ~10 of the finding's cited digest line numbers (audit-flagship-mock, audit-naval, audit-ambient-ulm) and all matched exactly, including the Ottoman ×6/Portugal ×6/Denmark ×6/Saxony ×6/Hesse ×5/PapalStates ×5 counts in audit-flagship-mock, which I counted by hand from the full turn-by-turn grep. The fix_shape is the right seam and is implementable with no signature changes: `_cooldown_keys` already receives `world`+`nation`+`recipient` and can derive `relation` the same way `_build_proposal_terms`'s friendly_gift branch does, then look up `_ASK_TARGET_STATE[base]` only for `proposal_type=="friendly_gift"` — this does NOT reintroduce the 'documented trap' the `apply_lapse_type_cooldown` docstring (ai_diplomacy.py:412-413) warns against, because that trap is about keying on the freely-rewritten `terms["type"]` for ANY proposal type (e.g. `design_purchase`, whose `terms["type"]` is an unrelated upgrade target), whereas the fix here is a narrow, hand-authored 2-way mapping scoped to exactly the one proposal_type (`friendly_gift`) whose base is always one of the four canonical ladder states. One correction to the evidence: `audit-latewar-t20/digest.md` has zero `LETTER` rows (grep -c returns 0), so the claim '8 of 9 arms' undercounts the exclusions — the true split is 7 of 9 arms show letters (tutorial and the turn-20 late-war fixture show none), and of those 7, `audit-propose` runs under an accept policy so it shows the title-collision on the FIRST ask only, not the repeat-decline cadence (it was correctly omitted from the finding's own citation list, just not from the '8 of 9' arm count). already_filed is honest: N30 (BUG_FIXES.md:1421, listed unranked/not-attempted at :1299) is the same seam and root cause, but N30 never identifies which labels collide or why, and has no fix_shape — this finding supplies the exact mechanism, an independently-reproducible repro, and a scoped one-seam fix, which is new enough to stand as its own actionable row (a maintainer should cross-link/merge with N30, not discard this).

findings.title: The muster's '… if all march' figure is an arrival-probability EXPECTATION, and the resolved commitment can EXCEED it with half the corps absent
findings._corrected: `_format_muster_lines` (combat_executor.py:1487-1496, not 1493-1498) prints `committed_strength` (built at combat_executor.py:1177-1178/1212 via `_committed_reinforcement_strength(..., expected_at=battle_region)`, combat_executor.py:445-496) under the label 'N if all march', but since PT-A2 that call weights every eligible joiner by its arrival-roll PROBABILITY (`_expected_arrival_weight`, combat_executor.py:1590-1611) rather than summing them at full weight — so the printed number is a probability-weighted mean, not the ceiling the label promises. Verified live on the 1805 boot: 'Ney (24,000; 78,676 if all march)' resolved to 'Massed effective strength: 24,000 (lead) + 60,266 committed (Davout, Lannes, Napoleon) = 84,266' with Murat (one of four WILL-JOIN candidates) absent — the resolved total exceeds the 'if all march' figure despite not every eligible corps arriving. Fix: at `_build_muster_preview` (combat_executor.py:1177-1212), also call `_committed_reinforcement_strength(marshal, will_join_marshals, world)` with `expected_at` omitted (the same resolver-semantics call already used at combat_executor.py:5869-5871) to get the true ceiling, thread it as `preview['attacker']['ceiling_strength']`, and render both figures in `_format_muster_lines`.
findings.summary: `_format_muster_lines` prints `committed_strength` as 'N if all march' (combat_executor.py:1493-1498), but since PT-A2 `committed_strength = strength + _committed_reinforcement_strength(..., expected_at=battle_region)` (:1206-1212) weights every eligible corps by its arrival PROBABILITY (:492-495, :1590-1613). The label promises a ceiling; the number is a mean. Verified by running on the 1805 boot: 'MUSTER — Ney (24,000; 78,676 if all march) vs Mack' resolved as 'Massed effective strength: 24,000 (lead) + 60,266 committed (Davout, Lannes, Napoleon) = 84,266' — 7% ABOVE the stated all-march figure while Soult, Murat and Bernadotte 'failed to reach the field'. Shown ≠ applied in the direction the label forbids.
findings.player_consequence: The one line the player commits from mis-states its own units: a cautious player reads 78,676 as the best case and is surprised by an 84,266 fight with three corps missing; conversely a player counting on 'all march' cannot tell how much of the number is a die.
findings.evidence: combat_executor.py:1493-1498 (label), :1206-1212 (expected_at), :445-509 (docstring: 'THE PREVIEW COUNTS ARRIVALS, NOT ELIGIBILITY'), :1590-1613, :7196-7200 (CO-6 line); in-process probe output 'MUSTER — Ney (24,000; 78,676 if all march)' and 'Massed effective strength: 24,000 (lead) + 60,266 committed (Davout, Lannes, Napoleon) = 84,266.'; PLAYTEST_FIXES_SPEC.md:101-124 (PT-A2 changed the number, kept the label). Verified by opening/running.

findings.already_filed: PT-A2 / CA9-F1 (BUG_FIXES.md:1177 'figure is qualified "if all march"') own the number; the label-vs-units mismatch and the measured over-ceiling resolution are NEW.

refuters.reason: Reproduced end to end. (1) Code read: `_committed_reinforcement_strength` (combat_executor.py:445-496) branches on `expected_at` — the resolver calls it with `expected_at=None` over `atk_participants` (the list of marshals who have ALREADY physically relocated into `battle_region` earlier in the same `_execute_attack` call, via `_calculate_reinforcements` + the arrival-roll relocation block at :5375-5440), treating each at full weight (certainty). The three preview call sites (:1177-1178 inside `_build_muster_preview`, :1428 the bad-odds modal, :1590-1611 `_expected_arrival_weight`) call it with `expected_at=<battle_region>` over the merely-*eligible* `will_join_marshals` list, multiplying each contributor's weight by `_expected_arrival_weight` — i.e. the arrival-roll's win probability. The docstring says so explicitly: 'Each contribution is scaled by the probability of the roll the resolver will actually make' (:474-475). So `preview['attacker']['committed_strength']` (:1212, built at :1177-1178) is a probability-weighted MEAN over the eligible set, not the resolver's true ceiling (sum-at-full-weight over the same set), and `_format_muster_lines` (:1481, label at :1487-1496) prints it under the words 'if all march', which promises a maximum. (2) Live reproduction (LLM_MODE=anthropic, default 1805 scenario, `Marshal Ney, attack Mack`) printed 'MUSTER — Ney (24,000; 78,676 if all march)…' and resolved with `reinforcement_messages` reading 'Massed effective strength: 24,000 (lead) + 60,266 committed (Davout, Lannes, Napoleon) = 84,266' while 'Murat could not reach the battlefield in time' (one of the four WILL-JOIN candidates absent) — 84,266 > 78,676, exceeding the printed 'if all march' figure despite not every eligible corps arriving. Numbers match the submitted finding exactly, confirming reproducibility rather than a one-off fluke. (3) Fix-shape check: `_committed_reinforcement_strength(marshal, will_join_marshals, world)` (no `expected_at`, i.e. `None`) computed at preview-build time would give the TRUE ceiling (ignores `.location`, so it does not require the candidates to already be at the battle region) — this reuses the same single-source function the resolver already calls with the identical semantics (:5869-5871), so it does not create a second implementation of the rule; it is the correct minimal seam. Only line numbers drift slightly from the submission: the label block is actually combat_executor.py:1487-1496 (not 1493-1498), the dict literal is combat_executor.py:1212 (matches), and the `_build_muster_preview` insertion point is combat_executor.py:1177-1178/1210-1212 (matches 1206 approximately). already_filed check: grepped BUG_FIXES.md and DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md — CA9-F1 (BUG_FIXES.md:1177, CLOSED as part of the 31-row CA9 landing) is the row that ADDED the 'if all march' wording, before PT-A2 (PLAYTEST_FIXES_SPEC.md:101-141, ROW PT build-complete Aug 12) changed the underlying number's semantics from a true sum to an arrival-probability-weighted mean without revisiting the label — so this finding is a genuine post-PT-A2 staleness, not a re-file of either closed row. tests/test_wo_slice8_panel_states_its_terms.py (WO slice 8, LANDED) discusses the same '78,676 if all march' figure but only to warn it is 'α-scaled, arrival-priced COMBAT WEIGHT, not a headcount' for a SUPPLY-billing purpose — it never questions the label-vs-ceiling mismatch for combat purposes, so it does not cover this claim.

findings.title: The vassal recovery hint is attached only while loyalty >= 40 — it disappears exactly when the bribe window opens
findings._corrected: vassal.py:711 `if delta < 0 and new_loyalty >= 40:` gates recovery_hint on the POST-delta loyalty, so it can vanish the same turn loyalty first drops below 40. Verified live: Switzerland drifting 39→37 emits 'satellite drift' with recovery_hint=='' and the paired dispatch.py:3808 'diplomatic_vassal_unrest' template ('Talleyrand reports unrest in {nation}.') carries no hint at all. Tracing the sibling producer shows the gap is a full dead zone, not merely cooldown-limited: Talleyrand's <35 advisory (dispatch.py:3435) only starts at loyalty<35 (strictly), so loyalty 35-39 gets zero hint from either producer — narrower than 'disappears at 39,' it is a hole between the two gates. attempt_vassal_bribe's window (loyalty<35, or <50 in an authority-grip spiral <30 — vassal.py:73-75, 2385-2386) confirmed reachable at loyalty 34 by direct call. Not a duplicate of BUG_FIXES.md F1/C1 (both closed, both about hint CONTENT/copy) or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md R132 (ledger display) — this is the GATE, unfiled.
findings.summary: process_vassal_loyalty attaches recovery_hint only `if delta < 0 and new_loyalty >= 40` (vassal.py:710-712). The AI bribe window is loyalty < 35 (or < 50 in a grip spiral) (vassal.py:73-75, :2380-2383). So the per-turn line names the levers when the satellite is at 98 and drops them at 39; the <40 dispatch event is the remedy-less 'Talleyrand reports unrest in {nation}.' (vassal.py:733-736, dispatch.py:3808). Talleyrand's <35 advisory (dispatch.py:3436-3455) names the hint but on a 3-turn cooldown, and the <=10 popup (vassal.py:740+) is never reached because the bribe lands first.

The imminent-rebellion popup, 'Empire Trembles' and the defection cascade never fire in practice: satellites are bought or conquered before loyalty reaches 20.

refuters.reason: Reproduced the exact mechanism by direct invocation (not just reading). At Switzerland loyalty 39→37 (SATELLITE drift, no other modifiers), process_vassal_loyalty(world) returned {'message': 'Switzerland loyalty 37 (-2): satellite drift', 'recovery_hint': ''} and the concurrently-queued world.pending_dispatch_events entry is exactly {'type': 'diplomatic_vassal_unrest', 'template_vars': {'nation': 'Switzerland'}} — whose template in dispatch.py:3808 is the bare 'Talleyrand reports unrest in {nation}.' with no hint slot at all. attempt_vassal_bribe(world,'Austria') at loyalty 34 (at-war, funded) is correctly reachable and rolls (returned a 'vassal_bribe_refused' event, i.e. the gate fired) — confirming BRIBE_ELIGIBLE_LOYALTY=35 / BRIBE_SPIRAL_LOYALTY=50 (vassal.py:73-75) is the real window, matching vassal.py:2385-2386's `loyalty >= BRIBE_ELIGIBLE_LOYALTY and not (in_spiral and loyalty < BRIBE_SPIRAL_LOYALTY)` skip-continue. The gate is exactly vassal.py:711 `if delta < 0 and new_loyalty >= 40:` (line number not stale) — and it reads the POST-delta new_loyalty, so it can even switch off on the very turn loyalty first drops under 40, a hair sharper than the finding stated. Tracing the sibling producer sharpens the finding further: Talleyrand's advisory at dispatch.py:3435 fires only on `elif loyalty < 35` (strictly), so loyalty 35-39 is a total dead zone — NEITHER the per-tick vassal_loyalty event (gated >=40) NOR the Talleyrand advisory (gated <35) attaches a hint there, worse than "cooldown-throttled coverage." Checked docs/BUG_FIXES.md rows F1 (2849) and C1 (2854): both are CLOSED and about hint CONTENT correctness (naming a blunted/nonexistent lever), not this GATE; DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md R132 (line 855) is about ledger trend-arrow display, also distinct. No open row covers the >=40 gate itself, so already_filed is correctly scoped as related-but-distinct. fix_shape's primary seam (drop/loosen the new_loyalty>=40 clause at vassal.py:711) is the right single point — it is the one gate whose removal restores hint coverage for both the per-tick event AND (once mirrored into template_vars) the dispatch line, without touching the already-fixed grip-aware CONTENT logic in recovery_hint_for_grip or Talleyrand's separate <35 advisory.

refuters.reason: Mechanism verified by opening all three cited files. war_status.py's contribution_share/contribution_overflow_count/standing_status_display fields are at lines 241-247 (not 244-249 — off by 3, likely from an earlier edit), confirmed via `grep -n` producing those exact keys. war_status_panel.gd:242 sets `row_btn.tooltip_text = _build_war_tooltip(war_data)` and `_build_war_tooltip` (line 302) is the sole reader of these three fields (confirmed via grep — no other reads exist in the file). war_detail_popup.gd genuinely has zero reads of 'contribution' (grep returned no matches), and its `show_war(war_data, ...)` (line 91) receives the SAME war_data dict passed to the HUD row — so the data is already present in-hand and `_render_war_detail` (line 350) simply never reads it while building its bbcode block from the same dict's other keys (breakdown, objective, naval_line, etc. — an identical pattern the fix would extend). This is not merely a UX nit: `docs/WAR_SETTLEMENT_ALLY_PARTICIPATION_SPEC.md` §16.2's UI-surfaces table explicitly requires "War status panel / war detail popup | Participant list, contribution shares, war bargain status, explanatory standing placeholder" — i.e. the spec mandates this on BOTH surfaces, and the popup implementation never got it. I also confirmed `material_contribution_share` is load-bearing for `get_coverable_enemy_participants` (settlement_validation.py:585, consumed by settlement_actions/offers/staging), substantiating the player-consequence claim that this figure gates who may settle. already_filed check reproduced: zero hits for 'contribution_share'/'Standing (top'/'standing_status_display' in BUG_FIXES.md or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md. The fix_shape (add a block to `_render_war_detail` reading the same dict keys, optionally sharing a row-formatter helper with the tooltip) is the correct minimal seam — no other rule needs touching, and it doesn't duplicate an existing implementation since war_detail_popup.gd currently has none. Only correction: line numbers.
