findings.title: Balance of Europe computes the threat projection (wars until a coalition brews/instant-forms) and never shows it
findings._corrected: diplomatic_ledger.py:1041 (war_exhaustion_trend build), :1061-1074 (threat_projection dict, matches coalition.py:41-42 THREAT_BREWING_MIN=60/THREAT_INSTANT_MIN=80), and :1115 (dissolution_threat_threshold, not :1096-1103 as originally cited) build threat_projection/wars_until_brewing/wars_until_instant/war_exhaustion_trend/hegemony_band/power_basis and a duplicate top-level coalition_posture key that godot-client/project-sovereign/scripts/diplomatic_ledger.gd's _render_balance_of_europe() (func at line 749) never reads (0 grep hits for any of those keys). Fix seam gd:846 (right after the threat bar) is correct. Note for the fix: the `after_next_war = threat_level + 20` figure (diplomatic_ledger.py:1061) only holds for a war declared WITHOUT casus belli — diplomacy.py:8264-8266 halves the threat gain to +10 when casus_belli is true, so the rendered projection line must say "up to +20 (+10 with just cause)" rather than assert a flat number.
findings.summary: diplomatic_ledger.py:1062-1074 builds `threat_projection` {current, after_next_war, brewing_threshold 60, instant_threshold 80, wars_until_brewing, wars_until_instant}, :1098-1103 `dissolution_threat_threshold`, and :1036-1041 a per-member `war_exhaustion_trend`; the Balance of Europe renderer diplomatic_ledger.gd:749-935 reads threat_level/threat_tier/threat_sources_this_turn/qualifying_nations/active_coalition.members[].war_exhaustion and nothing else (grep for threat_projection/wars_until/war_exhaustion_trend/dissolution in the .gd: 0 hits). The thresholds the projection quotes match the engine (coalition.py:41-42 THREAT_BREWING_MIN=60, THREAT_INSTANT_MIN=80; :49 DISSOLUTION_THREAT_THRESHOLD=20), so rendering would be shown=applied.
findings.player_consequence: The tab says 'Threat Level: 47 / 100 [MODERATE]' and lists this turn's sources, but never the one number a player plans around — 'one more war of conquest and a coalition brews; two and it forms at once' — nor which coalition member is tiring. refuters.reason:
Reproduced by opening both sides of the seam. Producer: backend/game_logic/diplomatic_ledger.py:1041 builds `war_exhaustion_trend` per coalition member; :1061-1074 builds the `threat_projection` dict (`current`, `after_next_war`, `brewing_threshold: 60`, `instant_threshold: 80`, `wars_until_brewing`, `wars_until_instant`) — literals 60/80 match `coalition.py:41-42` (THREAT_BREWING_MIN/THREAT_INSTANT_MIN) exactly; `hegemony_band` (line 1083), `power_basis` (1088) and a duplicate top-level `coalition_posture` (1097) are also built and returned. Consumer: godot-client/project-sovereign/scripts/diplomatic_ledger.gd `_render_balance_of_europe()` (func at line 749) reads threat_level, threat_tier, threat_sources_this_turn, qualifying_nations, coalition_state, brewing_turns_remaining, active_coalition.{name,leader,posture,combined_strength_display,members[].{nation,strength_display,war_exhaustion}}, war_exhaustion_max, paymaster_subsidy, dissolution_threat_threshold, dissolution_min_members, coalition_cooldown — confirmed by grep that threat_projection, wars_until_brewing, wars_until_instant, after_next_war, brewing_threshold, instant_threshold, war_exhaustion_trend, hegemony_band, power_basis, and the top-level coalition_posture key never appear in the file (0 hits). already_filed check: grepped docs/BUG_FIXES.md and docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for "threat_projection", "wars_until", "war_exhaustion_trend", and "Balance of Europe" — zero hits in both files, so "none" is correct. Fix seam (gd:846, `var sources = boe.get("threat_sources_this_turn", [])`) is verified as the line immediately after the threat bar render (bbcode += bar + "\n\n" a few lines above) — a sensible splice point, matching the finding's "~:846, after the threat bar" description exactly.

One nuance to fold into the fix: the projection's `after_next_war = threat_level + 20` literal is at diplomatic_ledger.py:1061 (not :1063 as stated), and it models the WORST case only — diplomacy.py:8264-8266 shows the real war-declaration threat gain is `10 if casus_belli else 20`, so a war fought WITH a casus belli only adds +10, not +20. The fix_shape's own caveat ("confirm the +20 literal equals the war_declaration threat increment") is itself only half-true and should be tightened to note the halving, or the rendered line should hedge ("up to +20, or +10 with just cause") rather than assert a single number as fact — otherwise the new UI text would be shown≠applied on the very case it's trying to fix.

findings.title: Corpus rows 'Ney, cover the retreat' / 'Ney, fix bayonets' pin a fast-parser refusal as a LIVE contract the prompt never made — the 527/531 live result is a corpus error, and the real PS18-5 harm has no live pin at all
findings._corrected: tests/data/parser_golden_corpus.json:3460-3481 assert `success:false` + 'Unknown action' on `world: any` with NO `mock_only` flag (verified by opening), while the eleven sibling rows that pin V2-55 fast-parser refusal shapes (e.g. :261-270 'break through enemy lines') carry `mock_only: true` with the note that the live LLM 'legitimately interprets the utterance'. The live layer cannot refuse these: PARSE_TOOL (providers.py:164-172) allows 'unknown' only 'when the prompt's rules forbid guessing', and the prompt's only such rule is the literal-delegation rule (prompt_builder.py:440-449); there is no guidance for a deed no action models (grep for cover/screen/bayonet in prompt_builder.py: none). So under --live the fast parser scores 0.5, the LLM is consulted, and it maps the sentence to the nearest Valid Action. The corpus is the wrong half. findings.title: Harness: a REFUSED dialogue answer is recorded as answered, so the driver never retries an offer after its blocker clears — the digest under-reports the AI's offers and cannot tell a stale-order refusal from a real one
findings._corrected: tools/playtest_driver.py:906-909 adds `did` to `_answered_dialogue_ids` BEFORE the POST reply is read; :931-935 then adds the refused word to `_refused_choices` keyed by dialogue id; `_dialogue_choice` (:987-1005) returns None once the only known word is refused → '(left standing)' (:904). So after the FA-28-style stale refusal the SAME offer, now legitimately active and re-derived by the safety valve on every response, is logged '(stale passthrough — #17 already answered this chain)' (audit-flagship-mock:132-133) and then '#17 → (left standing)' (:135), and lapses at end turn. Verified by opening. The driver also reads every popup key on one response as independent `if`s (scan(), :640-905) while the client renders a single route, so the digest never shows the client-side loss of FA-30.

findings.player_consequence: Not player-facing directly, but it hides player-facing facts from every memo: in the flagship 24-turn run four major-court offers (Russia armistice, Prussia open borders ×2, Britain armistice — audit-flagship-mock:135, :231, :267, :343) were answerable and lapsed unanswered, so the diplomacy pillar reads as 'the AI offers nothing France can take' when the truth is the harness stopped answering.
findings.evidence: tools/playtest_driver.py:892 (stale passthrough log), :904 (left standing), :906-909 (answered-set add before reply), :918-921 (refused note), :931-935 (refused memory), :970-985 (_refusal_key), :987-1005 (_dialogue_choice); digest lines above.
findings.repro: Run any scripted arm where a proposal and a settlement offer are both pending and a petition/advisory precedes them (flagship script turn 9); read digest.md for '(stale passthrough' followed by '(left standing)' on the same dialogue id.
findings.fix_shape: In the dialogue arm (driver:906-935): only add `did` to `_answered_dialogue_ids` and `_refused_choices` when `reply.get('stale_dialogue')` is falsy; on a stale refusal, leave the id un-answered so the next passthrough of that id is answered again (one retry per chain).
findings.behaviour_test: Driver unit test with a fake transport: first POST returns `{'success': False, 'stale_dialogue': True}`, the re-derived dialogue with the same id appears on the next response, and the driver POSTs again and records the second (successful) answer; a genuinely refused (non-stale) answer is still not repeated.

findings.title: Harness: ambient runs never see major-court proposals — the deferral rule plus a letter-book-only mailbox read means Prussia's recurring open-borders overture and Britain's settlement offer are invisible in every 'Europe acts' digest
findings._corrected: `_apply_command_popup_contract` (main.py:1353-1362) defers every choice popup on an `enemy_phase` response, so an end-turn-only run never receives `incoming_proposal`/`incoming_settlement_offer` on the wire; the driver's only mailbox read is `answer_envoy_digest((GET /mailbox).envoy_digest)` (driver:1320-1324, :939-970), which walks digest rows only — `is_routine_small_court` excludes majors by tier (envoy_digest.py:78-82) — and it never calls /pending_envoy or /mailbox/activate (grep: no such calls). `lapsed_offers` is set on the executor result (meta_executor.py:477-478) but no `/command` layer forwards it — main.py contains no `lapsed_offers` at all and `_COMMAND_RESULT_SIMPLE_FIELDS` (main.py:554-578) omits it. Verified by running a 10-turn end-turn-only TestClient probe: non-digest mailbox rows before end turn = Prussia open_borders on turns 2, 5, 9 and Britain settlement_offer from turn 4 on; envoy popups delivered on end-turn responses = 0; `lapsed_offers` on the wire = [] every turn.

findings.player_consequence: The archived ambient digests report the AI's diplomacy toward France as nonexistent: audit-ambient40 has POPUP=0 over 40 turns (LETTER=14 small-court rows only), audit-ambient-ulm POPUP=0 — while Prussia in fact courted France every ~4 turns and Britain tabled a persistent settlement offer. `--diplomacy accept` in ambient mode can therefore never accept a major-court offer, and any memo scoring 'AI aliveness' or 'diplomacy' from an ambient digest is reading a blind spot, not the game. findings.title: Mock-default vocabulary refuses the plainest hold/move phrasings and verb typos, and every refusal suggests attacking an ALLY ("Perhaps: 'Ney, attack Deroy'")
findings._corrected: In mock mode (no LLM fallback) the keyword chain (backend/ai/llm_client.py:1440-1620) has no stay/remain/rest keyword for hold or wait, no generic verb-typo tolerance (only four hard-coded 'build' misspellings at :1610 and ad hoc scout typos), and is missing 'advance on / push on to / onward to' move forms even though 'advance to' works — verified by direct reproduction of all eleven listed phrasings against the real 1805 boot world via TestClient, every one refused as 'Unknown action.' Separately, Berthier's mock recovery template (backend/ai/llm_client.py:897-899, `_berthier_mock_response`) picks its example enemy as `list(game_state['enemies'].keys())[0]`; `game_state['enemies']` is built in `get_llm_game_state()` (backend/main.py:211, dict at :236-244) filtered only by fog visibility (PARTIAL+), never by `is_at_war` — confirmed by opening `WorldState.get_enemy_marshals()` (backend/models/world_state.py:3543-3548), which excludes only the player's own nation, versus the unused `get_hostile_marshals()` (:3556) which does filter by war. On the shipped 1805 boot, `get_enemy_marshals()[0]` is Deroy of Bavaria — France's ALLIANCE partner, `is_at_war(France, Bavaria)` is False — reproduced live: the recovery text for both 'Ney, stay put' and 'Ney, forward!' literally reads "Perhaps: 'Ney, attack Deroy'", and reproducing that exact suggested command returns the refusal 'Ney cannot attack Bavaria — they are our ally, Sire, and we are not at war with them.' The correct single seam for the ally-suggestion half of the fix is `_berthier_mock_response`'s enemy-name selection, which already receives `game_state['world']` (threaded from `get_llm_game_state()` through `generate_berthier_recovery`, main.py:2865) and can filter by `world.get_hostile_marshals(world.player_nation)` there without touching the (correctly working) attack-refusal logic.
findings.summary: In the shipped mock mode (no LLM fallback) the chain has no stay/remain keyword (grep of llm_client.py: none), no verb-typo tolerance except four hard-coded build misspellings (llm_client.py:1610 'bould','biuld','buld','buid'), and no 'advance on / push on to / onward to' forms while 'advance to' works (the PS18-8 one-preposition shape). Berthier's recovery line then names `enemy_names[0]` from the fog-filtered `enemies` dict (llm_client.py:897-899, verified by opening), which main.py:237 fills from `get_enemy_marshals()` by VISIBILITY, not by war state — and on the 1805 boot entry 0 is Deroy of Bavaria, France's ally.
findings.player_consequence: Verified by running: `Ney, stay put`, `Ney, stay where you are`, `Ney, remain in Rhineland`, `Ney, don't move`, `Ney, rest your men`, `Soult, atack Mack`, `Ney, attak the austrians`, `Ney, advance on Swabia`, `Ney, push on to Munich`, `Ney, onward to Munich`, `Ney, forward!`, `Ney, take Swabia`, `ask Austria for a ceasefire` → all 'Unknown action'; the recovery copy reads "Perhaps: 'Ney, attack Deroy' or 'Ney, move to Paris'?" — and `Ney, attack Deroy` is itself refused: "Ney cannot attack Bavaria — they are our ally, Sire" (verified by running). Refusing is better than guessing, but the first hour of a mock player is spent rephrasing 'hold' and 'advance', coached toward an order the game will refuse.
findings.evidence: verified by opening backend/ai/llm_client.py:897-899 and :1475-1500 (wait/hold arms), :1500-1530 (move list), :1610; backend/main.py:237; verified by running the /command probes on the 1805 boot.
findings.repro: POST /command {"command":"Ney, stay put"} → 'Unknown action' with 'Perhaps: Ney, attack Deroy'; then {"command":"Ney, attack Deroy"} → 'they are our ally'.
findings.fix_shape: Three small arms, one file: (a) add `stay|remain|stay put|don't move|rest` → hold/wait and `advance on|push on to|onward to|forward to <region>` → move to the chain; (b) an edit-distance-1 pass over the verb keyword set for a single unknown token (reuse parser `_edit_distance_at_most`); (c) `generate_berthier_recovery` picks its example enemy as the first entry whose nation `world.is_at_war_with(player)` (fall back to the strongest visible belligerent).

findings.already_filed: NP-X9 (inflection tolerance → CR-6 proper, BUG_FIXES.md:809) is adjacent; stay/remain, verb typos and the ally suggestion are unfiled

refuters.reason: Every mechanism claim was independently reproduced. (1) grep of llm_client.py for 'stay'/'remain' returns zero keyword matches (only comments) — confirmed by opening the hold/wait branches at llm_client.py:1479-1489 (hold family: 'hold at all costs'...'guard'...'protect') and :1470-1473 (wait family: 'wait'/'stand by'/'pass'); no stay/remain form anywhere. (2) grep for edit_distance/fuzzy/levenshtein/typo in llm_client.py shows no generic verb-typo pass; the only misspelling handling is the four hard-coded 'build' typos at :1610 and ad hoc 'acout'/'scou' at the scout branch — confirmed by opening. (3) Ran the actual mock parser through TestClient on the real 1805 boot world and reproduced every claimed refusal verbatim: 'Ney, stay put', 'stay where you are', 'remain in Rhineland', "don't move", 'rest your men', 'Soult, atack Mack' (verb typo), 'Ney, attak the austrians', 'advance on Swabia', 'push on to Munich', 'onward to Munich', 'take Swabia' all returned Berthier 'cannot determine the order' responses — none resolved to hold/wait/move. (4) The Berthier recovery text for 'Ney, stay put' and 'Ney, forward!' both literally printed "Perhaps: 'Ney, attack Deroy'" — reproduced verbatim. (5) Opened llm_client.py:897-899 (_berthier_mock_response): enemy_names = list(game_state.get('enemies', {}).keys()); first_enemy = enemy_names[0]. Opened main.py:211-275 (get_llm_game_state): the 'enemies' dict is built from world.get_enemy_marshals() filtered only by PARTIAL+ visibility (main.py:236-244), never by war state. Opened world_state.py:3543-3548: get_enemy_marshals() returns 'all marshals NOT belonging to the player's nation' with no is_at_war check (a separate get_hostile_marshals() at :3556 does filter by war and is NOT used here). (6) Ran WorldState.from_scenario on europe_1805.json: get_enemy_marshals()[0] is Deroy/Bavaria, and is_at_war(France, Bavaria) is False; get_diplomatic_state(France, Bavaria) is 'ALLIANCE'. (7) Ran 'Ney, attack Deroy' through the live executor and reproduced the exact refusal text verbatim: 'Ney cannot attack Bavaria — they are our ally, Sire, and we are not at war with them.' Every element of the mechanism is exactly as described, not a stale line number or a misdiagnosed symptom. The fix_shape's arm (c) is the correct single seam: main.py:211 get_llm_game_state() already threads 'world' into the same game_state dict passed straight through to _berthier_mock_response (main.py:2865, generate_berthier_recovery -> game_state=llm_game_state), so deriving the example enemy from world.get_hostile_marshals(player_nation) at that one call site is reachable without restructuring, and fixes the display symptom without touching the (correct) attack-refusal executor logic. Arms (a) and (b) are reasonable extensions of the existing keyword-list pattern in the same file and don't duplicate any other rule found. already_filed is honest: BUG_FIXES.md:1781-1782 describes a DIFFERENT prior Deroy-adjacent bug (CA8-28's R5 destination-resolution guard wrongly keyed on war status instead of visibility for the 'march to join <marshal>' seam, now fixed) — different file/mechanism/consequence from this finding's cosmetic recovery-text example naming an illegal attack target; F11 (BUG_FIXES.md:1391, strategic_parser.py target-name fuzzy tolerance for PURSUE) is a different mechanism from the mock-parser VERB-keyword typo intolerance shown here (verified 'atack'/'attak' fail even though F11 claims 'attack is fully tolerant' for target NAMES, not verb spelling — no contradiction). NP-X9 (inflection tolerance, homed to CR-6 proper) is correctly flagged as adjacent-but-distinct. No existing open row covers the stay/remain gap, the verb-typo gap, the missing move-preposition forms, or the ally-suggestion defect.

findings.title: No headline class for the player's OWN peace — the war's end leads the briefing only when a corps happens to be stranded
findings._corrected: CONFIRMED and strengthened. `_build_headline`'s event-window loop (backend/game_logic/dispatch.py:429-1050ish, scanning `world.event_log`) has no `elif etype == ...` branch for `diplomatic_treaty_signed`, `peace_ratified`, or `armistice_expired_peace` — verified by reading the whole loop (region_captured/nation_eliminated/marshal_captured/marshal_destroyed/retreat/battle/war_declaration/evacuation_granted/evacuation_lapsing/crisis_brewing/crisis_passed/third_party_peace/coalition_formed are the only cases; the state-based candidates that follow — enemy_on_our_soil/estate_eroding/supply_strain/levy_open/marshal_reversal — don't touch it either) and by two direct reproductions. Reproduction 1 (bare `set_diplomatic_state(w,'France','Britain','PEACE')`, matching the finding's own repro): headline None, diplomatic_events [], peace_settlements None — expected, since `set_diplomatic_state` alone bypasses `_ratify_treaty`/`peace_ratification_log` entirely (world_state.py:10231 `is_player_treaty`, :10945-11044, the block that actually logs `diplomatic_treaty_signed`/`peace_ratified` and appends to `peace_ratification_log`, is INSIDE `_ratify_treaty`, called from `diplomatic_executor.py:5458/:6394` — the real production accept-peace seam — not from `set_diplomatic_state`). Reproduction 2 (stronger, decisive): manually seeding a rich `peace_ratified` event (french_victory, +55 score, Hanover gained) into `world.event_log` PLUS a matching `peace_ratification_log` entry — `build_morning_dispatch` still returns `headline: None` while `peace_settlements` independently renders a polished sentence ('The Treaty of London — France and Britain have concluded peace after 12 turns of war. France gained Hanover. Final war score: +55.', built by `_build_peace_settlement_section` at dispatch.py:3661-3690, exposed at :2142-2144). So even a clean, decisive, player-won peace with territory gained never becomes the dispatch's lead sentence — the exact right sentence is already computed and sitting in a separate, non-headline field. `armistice_expired_peace` (diplomacy.py:9890-9908) is a THIRD, independent event source with the same gap, reachable for ANY pair (not gated to `is_player_treaty`) — its notification text also assumes the player is always one of the two nations, a related but separate latent bug not part of this finding. The digest citation (audit-propose/digest.md:234,245) checks out exactly: Austria's peace is announced only via `road_home` a turn later, and only because Austrian corps happened to be stranded on French soil — a bare peace with no stranded army (my Repro 1) produces nothing at all, matching the finding's core claim. `already_filed: none` confirmed by grep of BUG_FIXES.md/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md (no row mentions peace_ratified/diplomatic_treaty_signed/armistice_expired_peace/"war is over"/"war's end"/"Treaty of"; WIN-D3's WIN-H5 row and WO-D5 are unrelated). Fix_shape is directionally right (one new headline class, ~weight 71, gated `player_nation in (nation_a,nation_b)` / `is_player_treaty`, reading the three named event types) but can be simplified further than proposed: since `_build_peace_settlement_section` (dispatch.py:3661) already composes the exact right sentence from `world.peace_ratification_log` for the `_ratify_treaty` path, the cleanest single seam is to have `_build_headline` promote that section's own entry (when present for the previous turn) into a candidate, rather than re-deriving a fresh template from the raw event fields — one fewer template to keep in sync, and it automatically inherits the ARMISTICE→PEACE vs WAR→PEACE phrasing already written there. `armistice_expired_peace` still needs its own `_add()` case since it has no `peace_ratification_log` entry. Minor citation drift only: HEADLINE_WEIGHTS table is dispatch.py:57-157 (not 54-157); everything else (2719, 9890-9908, withdrawal.py:470-530 rollback, world_state.py:10945-11044) checks out at the cited or immediately-adjacent lines.
findings.summary: `HEADLINE_WEIGHTS` (dispatch.py:57-159) has `war_touches_us` (70) for a declaration or coalition but no mirror for a war ending. The only peace-adjacent class, `road_home` (:806-813, template 'Sire — the war with {other} is over. {line}'), is raised from `evacuation_granted`, which withdrawal.py:530-537 returns from WITHOUT logging when no corps is stranded. The body does carry the peace (`diplomatic_treaty_signed` queued at world_state.py:10975; `peace_settlements` built at dispatch.py:2142 and rendered by main.gd:3305/3511), so it is not silent — but the lead is. In audit-propose the acceptance landed on turn 22's end-turn ('Austria has accepted our Peace Treaty!', digest.md:236) with the turn-23 dispatch 'Provence has fallen' (:238) and the peace led only at turn 24 (:243) because Massena stood abroad.
findings.player_consequence: The player who spends three turns of DP suing for peace can sign it and open a briefing whose first line is a supply nag; whether 'the war is over' ever leads depends on where his marshals happen to be standing, not on the peace.

findings.title: No per-corps march cadence: one AI corps captures three homeland provinces per enemy phase while the player's own standing march moves one
findings._corrected: DUPLICATE-ADJACENT to PT-D4 (`DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md`, LANDED Aug 1 2026, `backend/main.py:1020 _collapse_enemy_move_chains`): P4.5's undefended-capture chain (enemy_ai.py:1039 round-robin loop → `_find_undefended_capture` enemy_ai.py:3380, single-hop scan of `adjacent_regions`, returns `{"action":"attack",...}` at :3498; prose at combat_executor.py:5034 inside `_execute_attack` def :4112) is mechanically confirmed and reproducible (player chain of 3 tactical `move`s costs AP 4→1 with no per-hop cap — GR5 holds; France boots with garrison only at Paris/Normandy/Flanders across 28 provinces). The player's *standing strategic MOVE_TO* order (not manual tactical commands) is the throttled side: `strategic.py:1005` caps a ONE-per-turn tick to `movement_range` hops (`process_strategic_orders`, called once per player turn, turn_manager.py:270). PT-D4 already shipped a presentation-layer fix for "chaining moves reads as teleportation," but its `_move_chain_event` gate (main.py:622-634, pinned by `tests/test_enemy_phase_presentation.py::test_own_non_move_action_breaks_the_chain`) treats any `action != "move"` as a chain-breaker, so P4.5's `action:"attack"` captures are never collapsed — exactly why the cited digests still show separate un-collapsed "marches... unopposed!" lines. The correct, cheapest fix is extending `_move_chain_event` to also match a successful uncontested "attack" capture (view-layer only, PT-D4's own idiom); alternatively extend `occupation_started` (gated on `has_building("fortification")`, `_attempt_region_capture` combat_executor.py:8287/8309) to homeland provinces for a real mechanical cadence fix — this is the sound existing seam, shared by PF-3's move-capture, the unopposed-attack arm, and the AI alike. Do NOT reuse `moved_this_turn`/`acted_this_turn` as fix_shape (a) suggests: `moved_this_turn` is artillery-only today but read unguarded at combat_executor.py:845/938 (auto-reinforcement Rule 12), jealousy.py:705, and marshal_voice.py:118/135 — setting it for every marshal's move would ripple into reinforcement eligibility and narration campaign-wide. `marshal.attacks_this_turn`/`increment_attacks_this_turn()` (marshal.py:1010-1025, an existing 0/10/20/30% per-attack fatigue ladder never invoked inside `_execute_attack`'s unopposed-capture arm) is the better-fitting unused seam if a mechanical throttle is wanted instead of extending occupation.
findings.summary: Tactical `move` and the unopposed `attack` capture cost 1 AP each and carry no per-marshal-per-turn gate: `_execute_move` sets `moved_this_turn` only for artillery (movement_executor.py:551-552) and `acted_this_turn` (:556), which nothing reads as a movement gate; `_execute_attack`'s unopposed arm (combat_executor.py:5008-5034 'marches from … into … unopposed!') and PF-3's move-capture (movement_executor.py:588-612) flip the province on every hop. The enemy AI's P4.5 undefended-capture rung (enemy_ai.py:1998 → `_find_undefended_capture` :3380) is picked inside the per-nation `while actions_remaining > 0` loop (:1039) with round-robin fairness, so a nation with one corps spends all its AP on it. Verified by running (probe D): the PLAYER can do the same — 'Ney, move to Lorraine' / 'move to Franche-Comte' / 'move to Lorraine' all succeed in one turn, AP 4→1 — so GR5 holds, but the player's strategic MOVE_TO is capped at `movement_range` hops per turn (strategic.py:1010 `for _ in range(regions_to_move)`), and France's 28 provinces boot with a garrison only at Paris/Normandy/Flanders (verified by running), so a landed corps walks the interior at ~45 men per hop. Archived: audit-latewar-t20 T20 'Paget marches from Berry into Gascony unopposed! (95 lost to march) Captured: France → Britain · Paget marches from Gascony into Guyenne unopposed! (46 lost to march) … · Paget marches from Guyenne into Anjou unopposed! (46 lost to march)…', T21 Anjou→Maine→Brittany, T27 Normandy→Artois→Picardy→Ile-de-France; audit-naval T19 'ArchdukeCharles marches from Piedmont into Provence unopposed! … · ArchdukeCharles marches from Provence into Lyonnais unopposed!'. The occupation-takes-turns machinery already exists for FORTIFIED provinces (`capture_result['occupation_started']`, combat_executor.py:5037) and is the natural cadence seam.
findings.player_consequence: A 5,000-man landing party overruns nine French homeland provinces in five turns with the dispatch reading 'X has fallen' every morning, while the player's own 'march to' orders crawl one province a turn; the only counter — a 2-AP garrison detachment per province — is invisible as such. It reads as the AI cheating even though the executor is symmetric.

Core mechanism CONFIRMED by reading + reproduction: enemy_ai.py's round-robin loop (`while actions_remaining > 0`, enemy_ai.py:1039) re-selects the same marshal within one enemy phase; P4.5's `_find_undefended_capture` (enemy_ai.py:3380, return at :3498 `{"action":"attack","target":best_target}`) scans only the marshal's CURRENT `adjacent_regions` — one hop — with no per-marshal-per-turn cap, so repeated 1-AP captures chain freely. The unopposed-capture prose lives at combat_executor.py:5034 (`"{marshal.name} marches from {old_location} into {resolved_target} unopposed!"`), inside `_execute_attack` (def at :4112). Player-side reproduction ran clean: `Ney` chained move→Lorraine, move→Franche-Comte, move→Lorraine, AP 4→3→2→1, all `success:True` — confirming GR5 (single actions are symmetric). The player's AUTOMATED equivalent — a standing strategic MOVE_TO order — genuinely IS throttled: `strategic.py:1005` `regions_to_move = getattr(marshal,'movement_range',1)` caps ONE per-turn tick of `process_strategic_orders` (docstring "Called at START of player's turn... BEFORE advance_turn()", strategic.py:213; sole caller turn_manager.py:270). Boot garrison confirmed by running: France 28 provinces, garrison only Paris 25000/Normandy 12000/Flanders 12000. Digest quotes for T20/T21/T27 (audit-latewar-t20) and T19 (audit-naval) match verbatim.

Two corrections change what should ship:

(1) `already_filed: "none"` is WRONG. `DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md` row **PT-D4** (LANDED Aug 1, 2026) is directly on point for this exact complaint — "One corps chaining 3–4 moves per enemy phase reads as teleportation... loudest contributor to enemy phase as theater: 5.5" — built as `backend/main.py:1020 _collapse_enemy_move_chains`. But its stitching predicate `_move_chain_event` (main.py:622-634) returns None whenever `ai_action.get("action") != "move"`, and `tests/test_enemy_phase_presentation.py::test_own_non_move_action_breaks_the_chain` PINS any "attack" as a chain-breaker by design (verified — grepped and read both). Since P4.5 issues undefended captures as `action:"attack"` (not `"move"`), they are NEVER collapsed, exactly why the archived digests still show 3 separate un-collapsed "marches... unopposed!" lines rather than one forced_march entry. So this is a real, narrower, still-open GAP IN A LANDED FIX, not a fresh defect — and the cheapest fix is extending `_move_chain_event` to also match a successful uncontested "attack" capture (same events[] from/to shape as a move), fully in PT-D4's own idiom, at the view layer only, zero mechanic change.

(2) fix_shape (a) is under-specified in a way that would break siblings. `moved_this_turn` (movement_executor.py:552) is set ONLY for artillery today but is read UNGUARDED (no artillery check) at combat_executor.py:845 + :938 (Rule 12 auto-reinforcement eligibility — "troops cannot force-march twice"), jealousy.py:705 (`_engaged` detection for the literal-doctrine hold counter) and marshal_voice.py:118/135 (post-battle narrative "holds at X, per your orders"). Setting it True for every marshal's every move (not just artillery), as fix (a) implies by name-dropping the flag, would silently change auto-reinforcement eligibility and dispatch narration campaign-wide — a much bigger, untested blast radius than "cap hops." A cleaner existing seam: `marshal.attacks_this_turn` / `increment_attacks_this_turn()` (marshal.py:1018-1025) already carries an escalating fatigue ladder (marshal.py:1010-1017, 0%/10%/20%/30% for the 1st–4th attack) built for exactly this "repeated action within a turn" concept — and is confirmed NOT called anywhere inside `_execute_attack`'s body (no `increment_attacks_this_turn()` call between def :4112 and the next `def` at ~5200+), so repeat unopposed captures pay zero fatigue today. fix_shape (b) — extending `occupation_started` (gated on `region.has_building("fortification")`, `_attempt_region_capture` at combat_executor.py:8287, gate :8309-8310) to homeland provinces — remains sound: it is the one shared seam PF-3's move-capture, the attack-arm's unopposed capture, and the AI all already call, so widening it is genuinely GR5-clean and the stronger of the two options as filed.

findings.title: Settlement-unavailable reason is computed for the War Detail row and never rendered — 'Open Settlement' just vanishes
findings._corrected: war_status.py:250-264 attaches settlement_eligibility/settlement_disabled_reason/settlement_disabled_reason_display/war_detail_actionability to every war row, and no .gd file (0 of 55) reads any of them; war_detail_popup.gd:108-109's `if settlement_available: _add_settlement_button(...)` has no else, so the button silently vanishes with no rendered reason (confirmed against the Request Terms disabled+tooltip idiom at :556-569, which the settlement button lacks). BUT the reason this fires is never 'settlement_dialogue_active' — war_status.py:773 always passes `ignore_active_dialogue=True` into `evaluate_open_settlement_eligibility`, and `_settlement_dialogue_active` (settlement_routes.py:99) matches only the SAME war_id besides, so 'Resolve the current settlement review first.' can never appear in this field for any row. The reachable, unrendered reasons are `not_side_leader` ('Only the war leader can settle this side.', settlement_validation.py:990) when France is a coalition member but not that side's leader, or `no_unresolved_hostile_pairs`/`no_coverable_enemy` (settlement_validation.py:996/1002) when a multi-party war's live pairs have individually resolved but the umbrella instance is still open — either should replace the repro.
findings.summary: war_status.py:252-265 attaches `settlement_eligibility`, `settlement_disabled_reason` and `settlement_disabled_reason_display` (vocabulary display_names.py:813-829: 'Resolve the current settlement review first.', 'Only the war leader can settle this side.', 'Multiple wars with this court; select a specific war…', 'This war state has changed; reopen settlement review.') to every war row, explicitly 'for the War Detail popup'. findings.title: The alliance-paradox block names a route France cannot execute and omits the one the executor exempts; the Cabinet's 'Propose Peace' row stays green while its send is structurally blocked
findings._corrected: CONFIRMED core mechanism, NARROWED framing: propose_peace never appears as a wizard action while state=="WAR" (diplomacy.py:10987 shows propose_armistice is the ONLY proposal row added in that branch; verified by running get_available_diplomatic_actions on the 1805 boot). The real gap is one state later: once the player follows the game's own counsel and signs an ARMISTICE (Bavaria remaining allied to France and at war with Austria), get_available_diplomatic_actions's `elif state == "ARMISTICE":` branch (diplomacy.py:11093) adds propose_peace via `_proposal_action` (diplomacy.py:10839-10944), which never calls get_peace_commitment_conflicts — so the wizard PREVIEW row shows available:True/no reason (verified by running), even though sending it will always HARD_STOP at diplomatic_executor.py:3908-3935's paradox gate (verified: identical block text). WIN-1 (BUG_FIXES.md:774, FIXED) already disables execute_proposal and states the reason once the player opens the confirm dialogue (verified: generate_dialogue at diplomatic_dialogue.py:857-895 does exactly this for both WAR- and ARMISTICE-state mounts) — the surviving gap is that the PREVIEW row itself, and its block text, are not honest: the row should arrive disabled/reason-stated at the wizard level per this project's own stated discipline, and the block text at diplomatic_dialogue.py:868-873 ("Settle the war jointly at the settlement table, or resolve Bavaria's war first") should not uniformly suggest "propose an armistice" as a fix, since the only state from which this text is reachable via the wizard (ARMISTICE) is one where the player already has an armistice. Also correct: the archived audit-propose/digest.md shows 7 total refusals (2 vs Austria, 5 vs Britain), not "6× turns 1-7"; Austria's peace succeeds at turn 7 (well before the eventual turn-22 accept) with no refusal; and there is no digest evidence Bavaria was "eliminated" — the finding's own cited probe tuple shows Bavaria|France went ALLIANCE→PEACE (de-allied, not conquered), which is what exits the paradox's ally-state check (diplomacy.py:4670), contradicting the finding's elimination narrative.
findings.summary: WIN-1's honest-availability fix is real and verified: the peace mount computes `get_peace_commitment_conflicts` and disables `execute_proposal` with the reason (diplomatic_dialogue.py:857-895), and the client honours `available:false` and renders warnings (proposal_confirm_popup.gd:211-223, :367-375). But the counsel reads 'Settle the war jointly at the settlement table, or resolve Bavaria's war first' (diplomatic_dialogue.py:868-873): France cannot sign for Bavaria, and the ARMISTICE — which the executor explicitly exempts from the paradox as 'the very armistice ladder the game's own counsel recommends' (diplomatic_executor.py:3908-3919) and which is the wizard's FIRST war-state row (diplomacy.py:10987) — is not named. Meanwhile `_proposal_action('propose_peace')` (diplomacy.py:11095) gates only cooldown/armistice/relations/anti-renewal/oathbreaker/cap and never consults the paradox, so the wizard row is `available: true` for a send that can never succeed.

In audit-propose the paradox refused Austria/Britain peace 6× over turns 1-7 and only lifted when Bavaria was ELIMINATED (probe: Austria|Bavaria WAR→PEACE and Bavaria|France ALLIANCE→PEACE on the same turn).

refuters.reason:
The core mechanism is real and I reproduced it end-to-end (diplomatic_dialogue.py:857-895 mount HARD_STOP, diplomatic_executor.py:3908-3935 send-gate exemption for armistice, get_peace_commitment_conflicts at diplomacy.py:4653). But two load-bearing claims in the finding are wrong on inspection of the very code and evidence it cites, and the fix_shape's suggested wording is broken for the actual reachable path.

(1) "The Cabinet's 'Propose Peace' row stays green while WAR" is FALSE. I ran get_available_diplomatic_actions(world,'Austria') on the 1805 boot (France at WAR with Austria, ALLIANCE with Bavaria, Bavaria at WAR with Austria): the only propose_* actions returned are propose_armistice and propose_white_peace — propose_peace is not in the list at all while state=="WAR" (diplomacy.py:10987 confirms this — it's the ONLY proposal row added in the `if state == "WAR":` block). propose_peace is appended only in the `elif state == "ARMISTICE":` branch (diplomacy.py:11093-11094). So GET /diplomatic_preview?nation=Austria while at war never shows this row at all; the finding's own cited evidence (diplomacy.py:10987, 11095) actually proves this, but the prose misreads it.

The real reachable defect is one step later than described: I set France-Austria to ARMISTICE (the counsel's own recommended route, with Bavaria still at WAR with Austria) and re-ran get_available_diplomatic_actions — propose_peace now returns available:True, disabled_reason:"" (verified by running). _proposal_action (diplomacy.py:10839-10944) indeed never calls get_peace_commitment_conflicts, so the wizard row is genuinely green at that point and the send would still HARD_STOP. This is the same bug, just one state later — a real, worse case than described, because it means WIN-1's mount-time disabling (BUG_FIXES.md:774, confirmed FIXED and working when I ran generate_dialogue directly) only fires once the player has already clicked into the confirm dialogue; the wizard PREVIEW row that should have been disabled per the project's own "honest availability" discipline (the same discipline WIN-1 itself invokes) is not.

(2) "only lifted when Bavaria was ELIMINATED" is unsupported by the cited digest and contradicted by the finding's own probe evidence. I read the full audit-propose/digest.md: there are 7 refusal lines total (2 vs Austria at turns 1 and 4, 5 vs Britain at turns 2/8/10/12/14 by line count), not "6× turns 1-7" as claimed. Critically, at Turn 7 `propose peace with Austria` SUCCEEDS (dispatches to Austria, no refusal — digest.md line ~93), three turns before the cited "index 4"/turn-22 acceptance, and there is no mention of Bavaria anywhere in the digest after turn 4 (no elimination, conquest, or annexation event). The finding's OWN cited probe result — `(Austria|Bavaria, WAR→PEACE)` and `(Bavaria|France, ALLIANCE→PEACE)` — says Bavaria's ALLIANCE WITH FRANCE ENDED (de-allied), which is what exits the paradox check at diplomacy.py:4670 (`if ally_state not in ("ALLIANCE","DEFENSIVE_ALLIANCE"): continue`) — not that Bavaria was eliminated. Bavaria still existed and was still (per the tuple) at peace with Austria afterward. This is an internal contradiction in the finding between its prose and its own cited evidence.

(3) The fix_shape's proposed replacement text — "propose an armistice — a truce carries no contradiction" — is broken for the actual reachable defect path: since the wizard's propose_peace row (and thus the paradox block) is only reachable from ARMISTICE state, the player already HAS an armistice when they hit this text; telling them to "propose an armistice" is nonsensical/redundant. The fix needs to be state-aware (at WAR: recommend the armistice route named explicitly; at ARMISTICE: recommend settling at the table or explain the truce will lapse into peace once Bavaria's own war ends) rather than one static string.

The already_filed note in the original finding is correct — WIN-1 (BUG_FIXES.md:774) is FIXED and does exactly what it claims (I verified the execute_proposal option really does arrive enabled:False with the reason attached, via a direct call to generate_dialogue). This finding is a legitimate, narrower follow-on to WIN-1 (the un-gated wizard preview row + the misleading/self-contradicting counsel text), not a duplicate, but its specific mechanism narrative (WAR-state visibility, elimination causality) needs correcting before a future engineer acts on it, or they'll go looking for a "Propose Peace row visible during WAR" that does not exist.

findings.title: The armistice preview promises a peace the thaw arithmetic cannot deliver: from the boot relations a single 5-turn truce always collapses back into war
findings._corrected: backend/game_logic/diplomacy.py:4368-4410 (build_war_context_snapshot's armistice_mechanics block) AND backend/game_logic/war_status.py:373-374 (armistice_projected_outcome, feeding war_status_panel.gd:359 / war_detail_popup.gd:511, the per-turn HUD) both project an armistice's outcome from relation_now >= ARMISTICE_AUTO_PEACE_RELATION alone, ignoring the turns remaining and the ARMISTICE_THAW_PER_TURN=3 thaw that runs every turn a truce is active (diplomacy.py:10411). Verified live: 3 turns into an Austria armistice (relation -71, 2 turns remaining), both the shipped check and a naive multiply-by-full-ARMISTICE_DURATION fix mispredict peace (projecting -56); the real outcome after the 2 remaining turns is -65, war resumes. A correct single-source projection must multiply the thaw rate by the REMAINING turns (already computed at diplomacy.py:4358-4362 as armistice_remaining_turns and at war_status.py:328 as remaining, defaulting to the full ARMISTICE_DURATION only when proposing fresh at elapsed=0), extracted into ONE helper both producers call rather than patched independently in two places.
findings.summary: `build_war_context_snapshot` projects the truce outcome from `relation_now >= ARMISTICE_AUTO_PEACE_RELATION` only ('Relations stand at −80 — unless they heal to −60 or better, the war resumes when the truce expires', diplomacy.py:4368-4380), while the only healing in a truce is `ARMISTICE_THAW_PER_TURN = 3` per turn (diplomacy.py:4090; :10411 `step = ARMISTICE_THAW_PER_TURN if state == 'ARMISTICE' else 1`) over `ARMISTICE_DURATION = 5` (:4064): −80 → −65 and −90 → −75, both below −60, so `process_armistice_expiry` (:9885-9942) resumes the war. The armistice is the one bilateral instrument exempt from the alliance paradox (diplomatic_executor.py:3911-3919), i.e. the ladder the game's own counsel recommends for Austria/Britain — and the preview never tells the player that one truce is arithmetically insufficient and a second is required (IGR-X3's own measurement: Britain −90 → −75 in one truce, peace only on the second).
findings.player_consequence: The player takes the counselled armistice with Austria (−80), reads 'unless they heal to −60 or better', watches five turns pass with nothing to do, and gets 'The armistice with Austria has collapsed. War resumes!' — the war score and battle records having been struck at the truce (the preview's own line says so). The number that would have told them (−65 at expiry) is never computed.
findings.evidence: verified by opening: backend/game_logic/diplomacy.py:4064, :4069, :4090, :4368-4410, :9875-9942, :10378-10411; backend/commands/diplomatic_executor.py:3911-3919; boot relations from tools/playtest_runs/probe-diplomacy-propose/saves/autosave.json `Britain|France: -90, Austria|France: -80` (verified by running the save dump). Docs: docs/BUG_FIXES.md §IGR-X3 (measured 'Britain −90 → −75 in one truce, a second reaching armistice_expired_peace').
findings.repro: Boot europe_1805.json; `build_war_context_snapshot(world,'France','Austria','armistice')` → `armistice_mechanics.projected_outcome == 'war'` with display line 'unless they heal to −60 or better'; sign the armistice (cheat or play), end 5 turns → `armistice_expired_war` at relation −65.
findings.fix_shape: ONE seam: the projection block at diplomacy.py:4368-4380 — compute `projected = relation_now + ARMISTICE_THAW_PER_TURN * ARMISTICE_DURATION`, set `projected_outcome` from it, and say it: 'Relations stand at −80 and will thaw to −65 by expiry — short of −60; the war resumes unless relations improve by other means, or a second truce follows.'
findings.behaviour_test: For relation −80 the armistice snapshot's `projected_outcome` is 'war' and a display line contains '-65'; for −72 it is 'peace' (−72 + 15 = −57 ≥ −60); pin `ARMISTICE_THAW_PER_TURN * ARMISTICE_DURATION` is what the copy uses (mutating the constant changes the printed figure).
findings.already_filed: none — IGR-X3 ✅ landed the thaw and removed the false 'waiting softens them' counsel, but the preview still does not do the arithmetic (grep 'armistice' rows in BUG_FIXES/DESIGN_REFINEMENT: no row on the projection).

refuters.reason:
Core claim confirmed by direct reproduction: diplomacy.py's armistice projection at diplomacy.py:4370 uses `on_course_for_peace = relation_now >= ARMISTICE_AUTO_PEACE_RELATION` (a snapshot of NOW), never the relation projected across the remaining truce, while `_process_relation_decay` (diplomacy.py:10411) actually thaws ARMISTICE pairs by ARMISTICE_THAW_PER_TURN=3/turn. I booted the 1805 scenario: France|Austria starts at -80 (matches the finding); signing an armistice and running the real decay 5 times lands relation at exactly -65 (matches the finding's arithmetic and IGR-X3's note that a second truce is needed). The alliance-paradox armistice exemption is also confirmed at diplomatic_executor.py:3917 (`if proposal_type == "peace":`).

Two things are wrong with the specifics, so this is NARROWED not CONFIRMED:

1. The proposed fix formula (`relation_now + THAW*ARMISTICE_DURATION`) is provably wrong once an armistice is already in progress. I simulated it: 3 turns into an Austria armistice (relation -71, armistice_remaining_turns=2, already computed at diplomacy.py:4358-4362), the naive full-duration formula projects -56 ("peace"), but running the real 2 remaining turns lands at -65 ("war" actually resumes). The multiplier must be the REMAINING turns, defaulting to the full duration only for a fresh (elapsed=0) proposal — the finding's literal recipe would ship a preview that is wrong in the mid-armistice case, which is the more common way this gets checked.

2. The "ONE seam" framing is false: there is a second, independent producer of the identical current-relation-only check at backend/game_logic/war_status.py:373-374 (`armistice_projected_outcome`), feeding war_status_panel.gd:359 and war_detail_popup.gd:511 — the persistent per-turn War Status HUD/detail popup, arguably the primary surface a player checks during an ongoing truce (more so than the one-shot proposal dialog diplomacy.py feeds). This producer always runs mid-armistice and already has `remaining` computed at war_status.py:328, unused at :373 — the same bug duplicated in a second place, exactly the "one rule, two implementations" failure this codebase's own CLAUDE.md flags as recurring.

findings.title: The strategic parser knows join / link up with / aid / assist / bolster as SUPPORT, but the mock chain only fires on reinforce/support — so "Ney, join Davout" is Unknown and "Ney, protect Davout" becomes a 2-AP HOLD 'at' a man
findings._corrected: strategic_parser.py:302-308 (dict key at 302, verb entries 304-308) lists \"come to the aid of\"/\"link up with\"/\"assist\"/\"aid\"/\"bolster\"/\"join\"/\"back up\"/\"shore up\"/\"rally to\"/\"combine with\" under SUPPORT, and the near-identical SUPPORT_OBJECT_PREFIX_RE (llm_client.py:101-105, not 104-109) recognizes the same verbs for CR-2 object-prefix stripping — but the mock action chain's only SUPPORT arm, llm_client.py:1598 (`elif \"reinforce\" in command_lower or re.search(r'\\bsupport\\b', command_lower): action = \"move\"`), only fires on \"reinforce\" or bare \"support\". parser.py's strategic-upgrade block (parser.py:1727-1785) only overwrites strategic_type/target on an already-resolved action and never assigns `command.action` itself, so with no base action set the other nine SUPPORT-family verbs all end in \"Unknown action\" end-to-end (verified via /command TestClient, not just parser.parse()), while \"protect\" (a HOLD keyword at llm_client.py:1485) turns \"protect Davout\" into a real 2-AP strategic HOLD order targeting the string \"Davout\". COMMAND_ROBUSTNESS_SPEC.md:92's citation of llm_client.py:1008-1022 for \"link up\" pre-emption is confirmed stale — that range is now cheat/debug parsing with no verb matching at all. Fix should reuse llm_client.py's OWN SUPPORT_OBJECT_PREFIX_RE verb alternation at line 1598 (no cross-file import needed, tighter single seam than exporting from strategic_parser) and let the HOLD arm yield to SUPPORT when guard/protect's object is a friendly marshal name; note \"cover\"/\"screen\"/\"follow\"/\"help\" (cited in the repro list) are not in either SUPPORT table and are a separate, unaddressed gap.
findings.summary: strategic_parser.py:302-308 lists "come to the aid of", "link up with", "assist", "aid", "bolster", "join" under SUPPORT, and SUPPORT_OBJECT_PREFIX_RE (llm_client.py:104-109) recognises the same verbs to protect the supportee from being bound as executor — but the mock action chain's only SUPPORT arm is llm_client.py:1598 `elif "reinforce" in command_lower or re.search(r'\bsupport\b', …)`. With no base action the strategic upgrade never runs (parser.py:1728 gates on a resolved order). "protect" is instead a HOLD keyword (llm_client.py:1485 "guard", "protect"), so "protect Davout" is a HOLD whose target is a marshal name. COMMAND_ROBUSTNESS_SPEC.md:92's claim that `link up` is pre-empted to move is stale.
findings.player_consequence: Verified by running: `Ney, join Davout`, `Ney, link up with Davout`, `Ney, aid Davout`, `Ney, help Davout`, `Ney, go help Davout`, `Ney, cover Davout`, `Ney, cover Davout's flank`, `Ney, screen Davout`, `Ney, follow Davout` → "Unknown action"; `Ney, protect Davout` → "Ney will hold Davout. Ney: 'Standing guard while others win laurels…' (2 AP — a standing strategic order to hold this ground…)" — 2 AP charged for a standing order named after a person; `Ney, support Davout` / `reinforce Davout` → SUPPORT correctly. The SUPPORT mechanic exists and half its natural vocabulary is unreachable in the shipped mock mode.
findings.evidence: verified by opening backend/ai/strategic_parser.py:296-312, backend/ai/llm_client.py:104-109, :1485, :1598, backend/commands/parser.py:1700-1732; verified by running the /command probes.
findings.repro: POST /command {"command":"Ney, join Davout"} → Unknown action; {"command":"Ney, protect Davout"} → 'Ney will hold Davout.' with 2 AP charged.
findings.fix_shape: ONE seam: make the llm_client.py:1598 arm read the SAME verb tuple strategic_parser's SUPPORT table uses (export it from strategic_parser and reference it), and let the hold arm yield to SUPPORT when the object after guard/protect/cover is a friendly marshal name.
findings.behaviour_test: each of join/link up with/aid/assist/bolster/come to the aid of/cover/screen + Davout → strategic_type SUPPORT, target Davout; `Ney, protect Davout` → SUPPORT not HOLD; `Ney, protect Rhineland` / `guard Lorraine` stay HOLD; golden-corpus rows for `support Ney`/`reinforce Davout` unchanged.
findings.already_filed: none

refuters.reason: Reproduced end-to-end, not just in parser.parse(). With LLM_MODE=mock and the real /command pipeline (backend/main.py TestClient), \"Ney, join Davout\" -> Berthier's in-character parse-failure line (\"Valid orders include: attack, move, scout, defend, fortify, recruit\"); \"Ney, aid Davout\" and \"Ney, come to the aid of Davout\" -> the generic \"I cannot parse this order\" refusal. Traced the exact mechanism: default action is \"unknown\" (llm_client.py:1364), the elif chain's only SUPPORT arm is `elif \"reinforce\" in command_lower or re.search(r'\\bsupport\\b', command_lower): action = \"move\"` at llm_client.py:1598 (line number exact), so none of join/link up with/aid/assist/bolster/come to the aid of/back up/shore up/rally to/combine with ever set a base action. parser.py's strategic-upgrade block (confirmed at parser.py:1727-1785, close to the cited 1700-1732) only ever OVERWRITES strategic_type/target on an already-resolved order — it never sets `command.action` itself — so even though strategic_parser.detect_strategic_command (PATTERNS[\"SUPPORT\"], confirmed strategic_parser.py:302-308) recognizes these phrases as SUPPORT-shaped text, the base \"unknown\" action wins and the whole request fails before the strategic layer's classification matters. \"protect Davout\" reproduced exactly as claimed: HOLD keyword list confirmed at llm_client.py:1485 (\"anchor at\", \"guard\", \"protect\"), and driving it through /command created a real strategic HOLD order targeting the string \"Davout\" (logged \"[STRATEGIC] Creating HOLD order for Ney -> Davout\", then an aggressive-personality objection — the 2 AP order genuinely exists, only intercepted by an unrelated objection roll in my probe). The COMMAND_ROBUSTNESS_SPEC.md:92 staleness claim also checks out: that line cites llm_client.py:1008-1022 for \"link up\" pre-emption, but that range is now cheat/debug-command handling and known-nation extraction (verified by opening) — no verb matching of any kind, so the spec citation is dead. already_filed correctly \"none\": grepped BUG_FIXES.md/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for SUPPORT_OBJECT_PREFIX, \"link up\", \"join\"+Davout, protect/HOLD collision — the one near-hit (PS18-8, \"head FOR Vienna\") is an unrelated destination-preposition fix that explicitly anchors itself to not shadow the SUPPORT family, so it is not a duplicate. Two refinements to the fix_shape, neither changing the verdict: (1) the more minimal single seam is IN THE SAME FILE — SUPPORT_OBJECT_PREFIX_RE already lives at llm_client.py:101-105 (not 104-109 as cited; off by ~3 lines) with almost the identical verb alternation used for CR-2's object-prefix stripping, so line 1598 could derive its condition from that regex's own verb group without a cross-module import from strategic_parser at all — an even tighter fix than the one proposed; (2) \"cover\", \"screen\", \"follow\", and \"help\" (included in the player_consequence repro list) are NOT members of strategic_parser's SUPPORT table or of SUPPORT_OBJECT_PREFIX_RE — their being Unknown is real (verified) but is a separate, uncited gap the proposed fix_shape would not actually close; the finding's fix only closes join/link up with/aid/assist/bolster/come to the aid of/back up/shore up/rally to/combine with.

findings.title: Three driver arms that do not exist and would answer the questions the archived arms cannot: the Negotiator, the Emperor Pays, and the Defended Homeland / LLM gauntlet
findings._corrected: Derived from what the eight archived arms structurally could not reach (each gap verified above): (1) THE NEGOTIATOR — `--diplomacy negotiate`: polls /pending_envoy and /mailbox items every turn, ACCEPTS counter-offers and settlement offers, walks `accept_settlement_offer` → settlement_confirm → confirm_settlement to ratification, and digests `peace_ratification_summary` (backend/main.py:588-600, a key the driver never reads) so a digest finally says WHAT was signed; today no unattended run has ever ratified a multilateral settlement or reached the Proclamation (NA-6 §17-§21 records say so), and the propose arm's only peace was a bare bilateral accept. (2) THE EMPEROR PAYS — a `--reward` policy: reads `response['notifications']` (backend/main.py:1412, unread by the driver) and, for reward rows, sends the row's `action_command` (UX23-A's `grant <name> a rente`) or `endow <name> with <eligible province>`; also types the rail's last-stand words ('fight to the last'/'attempt breakout') so a parked fate question (FA-36) is answered when raised. ES-7/UX23-A/Jealousy have never been measured unattended — ambient40 ends with 'Lannes's grievance is 34 turns old'. (3) THE DEFENDED HOMELAND + LLM GAUNTLET — a script that garrisons/holds the French homeland (so Paget's 3-provinces-a-turn walk in audit-latewar-t20 and Mack's march to Lorraine in the flagship are evaluated against resistance rather than vacuum) and, on `--llm anthropic`, a companion script of sub-0.7-confidence sentences (delegations, negations, conditionals, 'cover the retreat'/'fix bayonets' — the two corpus rows the live parser resolves to actions) with parse provenance recorded (FA-39), so a 'live' arm measures the live parser.

findings.title: Trafalgar cannot lead the Morning Dispatch
findings._corrected: Naval beats ('trafalgar'/'fleet_action', logged by `naval._log_fleet_action`, naval.py:1246-1261) reach the player ONLY through `queue_dispatch_event` → `world.pending_dispatch_events` → `_build_diplomatic_events_section` (dispatch.py:4339) as a DIPLOMATIC EVENTS rail line at priority HIGH (`_DIPLOMATIC_EVENT_PRIORITY["trafalgar"]`, dispatch.py:4073). The separate headline scorer `_build_headline` (dispatch.py:429) has no `_add()` call site for either event type and `HEADLINE_WEIGHTS` (dispatch.py:57) has no naval class at all, so a decisive fleet action can never be the morning headline — confirmed independently: across all 20 turns of docs/audits/playtest_digests/audit-naval/digest.md, zero DISPATCH lines ever mention Trafalgar/fleet/sail despite the fleet losing ~23 of 49 sail (digest lines 56→121) consistent with the turn-5 diversion interception (naval.py:1515). Correction to the original evidence: digest.md:88 is the turn-7 dispatch and is NOT 'the morning after' the turn-5 event (that event has already aged out of `_build_headline`'s 2-turn window, dispatch.py:437-438, by turn 7 regardless of the missing weight class); the true next-morning dispatch is digest.md:76, which also omits it. Fix_shape stands: add a `trafalgar` HEADLINE_WEIGHTS entry plus a matching `_add()` call inside `_build_headline`, mirroring the WO-D6 `capital_lost` precedent (dispatch.py:69-79). Not a duplicate of any BUG_FIXES.md/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md row (checked PC15-14 and WO-D3, both different defects).
findings.summary: Naval beats reach the dispatch only through `queue_dispatch_event` → the DIPLOMATIC EVENTS rail; `HEADLINE_WEIGHTS` has no naval class, so a decisive fleet action that halves the Combined Fleet can never be the lead. The morning after losing 46 coalition sail the headline was an allied province.
findings.player_consequence: The campaign-defining naval catastrophe reads as a footnote below 'Leon has been taken by Britain'; the war's biggest single loss of the run has no lead sentence.
findings.evidence: Verified by opening backend/game_logic/dispatch.py:57-140 (HEADLINE_WEIGHTS — no trafalgar/fleet/strait/expedition class; grep confirmed), :4157 (`queue_dispatch_event` appends to pending_dispatch_events), :4338 (`_build_diplomatic_events_section` renders them as rail lines), :4073 ('trafalgar': HIGH is the rail priority only), :3952 (the TRAFALGAR template). Verified by opening docs/audits/playtest_digests/audit-naval/digest.md:88 — verbatim turn-6 headline 'Sire — Leon has been taken by Britain.' the morning after the turn-5 `trafalgar` event (t7 snapshot event_log).

findings.fix_shape: ONE seam: add a `trafalgar` headline class to HEADLINE_WEIGHTS (~90, between region_lost 75 and marshal_captured 95) built by `_add` from the `trafalgar` event when the loser is the player's side; keep the rail line as the sub-beat.
findings.behaviour_test: After a decisive fleet action lost by the player, `build_morning_dispatch(world)['headline']['text']` contains 'TRAFALGAR'; after a non-decisive action it does not.
findings.already_filed: none

refuters.reason: Reproduced the mechanism by direct code read. `HEADLINE_WEIGHTS` (backend/game_logic/dispatch.py:57-155) has no naval-related key (checked every key by eye and by grep for trafalgar/fleet/naval/sail — none). `_build_headline` (dispatch.py:429) reads `world.event_log` and calls `_add(cls, ...)` from ~30 explicit, hand-coded sites (grep for `_add(` inside the function body, lines 429-1090) — none of them handle event type "trafalgar" or "fleet_action"; those two event types are logged by `naval._log_fleet_action` (naval.py:1246-1261) purely via `world.log_event(...)` (invisible to the headline unless a matching `_add()` exists) and `queue_dispatch_event(world, "trafalgar"/"fleet_action", ..., "always")`, which only feeds `_build_diplomatic_events_section` (dispatch.py:4339, off-by-one from the cited :4338) with priority `_DIPLOMATIC_EVENT_PRIORITY["trafalgar"]="HIGH"` (dispatch.py:4073, exact) — i.e. a DIPLOMATIC EVENTS rail line only, never the headline scorer. Structurally, a decisive fleet action can never be the lead sentence. This is corroborated even more strongly than the finding claims: grepping every `DISPATCH:` line across all 20 turns of docs/audits/playtest_digests/audit-naval/digest.md, zero ever mention Trafalgar/fleet/sail, despite the fleet visibly losing ~23 of 49 sail between turn 4 and turn 9 (digest lines 56 vs 121), consistent with `resolve_diversion`'s failure branch (naval.py:1515, `caught coming home... loses N sail`) firing at turn 5's 'order the diversion' command. One specific citation error in the original finding, however: digest.md:88 ('Leon has been taken by Britain') is the turn-7 dispatch (its 2-turn window per dispatch.py:437-438 covers only turns 6-7) — it is NOT 'the morning after' the turn-5 trafalgar event. The true next-morning dispatch is digest.md:76 ('Bernadotte's Counter-Punch opportunity has expired'), which also never mentions the fleet loss — by turn 7 the turn-5 event had already aged out of the 2-turn candidate window regardless of the missing weight class, so the specific correlation drawn is wrong even though the general conclusion (no naval headline, ever) is right and even better supported by the full digest than the single cited line. The fix_shape is correctly scoped: it names the one function that needs both a new HEADLINE_WEIGHTS entry AND a matching `_add()` call site inside `_build_headline`, which is exactly the established two-part pattern used for every other class in this file (e.g. the WO-D6 `capital_lost` precedent, dispatch.py:69-79, added for an identical class of missing-headline defect). Grepped docs/BUG_FIXES.md and docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for 'trafalgar'/'naval headline'/'fleet_action headline' — no existing row covers this; PC15-14 (BUG_FIXES.md:1145) is the opposite defect (a non-event wrongly leading), and WO-D3 (DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md:215) is about naval being an unused strategy, not the headline weight gap. Not a duplicate.

findings.title: Cooldown refusal prints the turns REMAINING as 'turns ago' ('rejected our last proposal only 1 turns ago') and names no wait
findings._corrected: `_execute_diplomatic_propose`'s cooldown refusal (backend/commands/diplomatic_executor.py:686 and the per-type sibling at :695) prints the DECREMENTING "turns remaining until re-proposal is allowed" value as if it were elapsed time since the rejection: `f"...{target_nation} rejected our last proposal only {remaining} turns ago."` The cooldown is set to 4 on rejection at world_state.py:10179 (:10182 for the `{target}_{ptype}` key — corrected from the cited 10186-10190, which lands a few lines below on the neighboring `apply_rejection_cooldowns`/`record_diplomatic_refusal` calls in the same REJECT branch) and is decremented toward zero once per turn by `CooldownManager.decrement_all()` (cooldown_manager.py:74-90), which deletes the key once it reaches 0 and reopens the gate at diplomatic_executor.py:682. So `remaining=1` means "one more turn until you may ask again," not "rejected one turn ago" — confirmed live in docs/audits/playtest_digests/audit-propose/digest.md at Turn 6 ('Russia rejected our last proposal only 1 turns ago.') and Turn 10 (Austria, same phrasing), and grammatically broken at 1 regardless. Every other reader of the same `player_proposal_cooldowns` dict in the codebase (diplomatic_ledger.py:401 comment, diplomatic_advisory.py:548, settlement_validation.py:431) treats the value as "remaining," and the sibling ultimatum-cooldown refusal at diplomatic_executor.py:3116-3117 phrases the identical decrementing-cooldown case correctly ("we must wait {ult_cd} more turns") — confirming this is an isolated wording bug in exactly the two f-strings named, fixable at that one seam without touching or duplicating any other cooldown-message implementation. Not previously filed (grepped BUG_FIXES.md/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for 'advises patience', 'turns ago', 'proposal_cooldown' — no matching row).

The cooldown gate at diplomatic_executor.py:682-687 (verified open) reads `remaining = cooldowns[target_nation]` and prints it as "...rejected our last proposal only {remaining} turns ago." Reproduced the backend mechanism exactly as described: a direct FastAPI TestClient sequence — POST /command "fortify" (state=awaiting_clarification) → POST /save → POST /load (response carries no `state` key, no clarification attach) → POST /command "Ney" — resolves to "[CLARIFICATION] Resolved answer 'Ney' -> 'Ney, fortify'" and returns Ney's objection to a fortify order never shown post-load. All cited lines check out: clarification.py:413-454 (register_pending_clarification builds a LOCAL_PLANNING dialogue and pushes/preempts it), main.py:2156-2178 (pops the dialogue and reinterprets the next typed line unconditionally), save_manager.py:217-240 (transient-clear block never touches dialogue_manager), main.py:4065-4143 (/load attaches WO-30/WO-35/WO-41 keys but nothing for command_clarification), main.gd:2397-2398 (`_response_has_clarification_route` gates strictly on `state=="awaiting_clarification"`). already_filed is correct — WO-35 (BUG_FIXES.md:705) only names pending_objection/pending_interrupt, and no BUG_FIXES/DESIGN_REFINEMENT row covers command_clarification.

However, the stated PLAYER CONSEQUENCE is not reachable through the shipped client and must be corrected. `clarification_popup` is registered as a MODAL dialog (main.gd:435, `dialog_manager.register(name, path, modal=true)` — default true), and while it is visible: `_show_clarification_popup` (main.gd:5093-5096) calls `set_input_enabled(false)` which sets `command_input.editable=false`, `send_button.disabled=true` AND `end_turn_button.disabled=true` (main.gd:3932-3937) — so the player cannot type, submit, or even end the turn while the question stands. Both known routes to the pause menu are also blocked: the ESC handler's pause-open branch is gated `elif not _is_modal_dialog_open():` (main.gd:992), and the top-bar gear button's `_on_top_bar_menu_clicked` has the identical `not _is_modal_dialog_open()` guard (main.gd:5372-5382) — `_is_modal_dialog_open()` delegates to `dialog_manager.is_any_modal_open()` (main.gd:5329-5335), which is true because `show_clarification()` calls `show()` (clarification_popup.gd:73) making the registered node visible. So Save is unreachable via the pause menu while the popup stands. Autosave can't capture this state either: it fires only once, at the START of a new turn (save_manager.py docstring), before any mid-turn clarification can exist, and reaching a NEW turn requires end_turn, which is disabled by the same modal gate; even if it weren't, submitting anything (including "end turn") through the answer-interpretation path pops/clears the pending clarification before parsing resumes (clarification.py's "pass" branch + main.py:2163's unconditional `.pop()`). There is also no save-on-quit handler (pause_menu.gd:127 is a bare `get_tree().quit()`), so force-closing the client does not persist the state either. The finding's own repro bypasses all of this by driving `/command`/`/save`/`/load` directly via TestClient — a path no shipped-client interaction can reach.

The fix_shape's seam is also slightly off: the codebase's own precedent for "discard a stale LOCAL_PLANNING dialogue type at load" already lives in `WorldState.from_dict` (world_state.py:7718-7725, the `conflict_alert` migration via `dm.remove_matching(...)`, right after `DialogueManager.from_dict` is restored) — not in `save_manager.py`'s transient-clear block. Since `save_manager.load_game` is the sole production caller of `WorldState.from_dict` (verified: only one non-test call site), the two locations are reachability-equivalent today, but housing the fix beside the existing analogous rule in world_state.py avoids splitting "clear a stale dialogue on load" across two files.

findings.title: AI marshals' trust is read by nothing on the AI path, yet the AI pays rentes and gives away provinces to stop an erosion that never bites it
findings._corrected: `_process_dotation_state` erodes ALL nations' marshals (world_state.py:6075 loop, GR5) and enemy_ai.py spends on `grant_dotation`/`grant_pension` to close shortfalls (enemy_ai.py:5722-5760; ambient40 digest lines 37, 47, 232 show the AI verbs firing). But trust's only mechanical readers are player-side: objections skip enemy marshals (`is_player_action_check`, executor.py:1130-1175), defiance rides objections (defiance.py:41-47), severity.py:118-125 feeds objections, and `grep -n trust backend/ai/enemy_ai.py` finds only a comment (line 194).
