findings.title: Berthier's battle observation is drawn with unseeded `random.choice`, so one enemy phase can print the same observation twice while enemy voice rotates
findings._corrected: `_pick_observation` (backend/game_logic/battle_report.py:617, invoked from combat.py:1022/1463 inside the world-independent `CombatResolver.resolve_battle`) draws Berthier's after-battle line via unseeded `random.choice` across ~30 priority-branch banks, causing verbatim repeats within one enemy phase when the same priority branch fires twice for the same marshal pair — reproduced in docs/audits/playtest_digests/audit-latewar-t20/digest.md:112 and :115, identical "lost_despite_terrain" line against Archduke Charles. XR-5 (BUG_FIXES.md:2995, closed) fixed the identical class of defect in `enemy_voice.py` only, via the REGION-keyed `_voice_rotation_key(world, target_location)` helper (combat_executor.py:257-266, already shared by enemy_voice at :6307 and marshal_voice at :6338) — `battle_report.py`'s Berthier bank was never migrated to it, and there is no "pair key" anywhere in the codebase (battle_counts is region-keyed, not marshal-pair-keyed). The fix is not a self-contained edit inside `_pick_observation`: because `generate_battle_report` is called from inside combat.py's world-independent `resolve_battle()` (no world/region parameter in its signature), the deterministic index must either be threaded down through that signature or — matching this file's own documented "glue it on at the executor seam" pattern (see `compose_campaign_cost_note`'s docstring, battle_report.py ~1010-1013) — applied at combat_executor.py by having `_pick_observation` expose which bank it selected so the already-computed `_voice_rotation_key` value can pick the index there, reusing the existing region-keyed mechanism rather than inventing a new one.
findings.summary: `_pick_observation` selects with `random.choice(_OBSERVATIONS[...])` (`battle_report.py:748-814`; `import random` at :11, no `random.seed` anywhere in backend/), whereas XR-5 gave `enemy_voice` a deterministic rotation on the serialized `battle_counts`. The observation IS rendered in the enemy-phase dialog ('Berthier: "…"', `enemy_phase_dialog.gd:492-495`). In audit-latewar-t20 turn 28, four Austrian attacks on Massena produced 'The hills were ours, but Archduke Charles took them. Massena's position was overrun.' twice in the same phase (digest lines 112 and 115; bank text at `battle_report.py:340`). Being module RNG it also varies across replays of the same `campaign_seed` (display-only, GR6-safe, but it is the one narration surface the AI-0b determinism work did not reach).
findings.player_consequence: On a multi-attack night the staff's one editorial line per battle repeats verbatim under consecutive battles, which reads as a stuck record in the very dialog CA8-7 made the antagonist's stage.
findings.evidence: verified by opening backend/game_logic/battle_report.py:11, :307-345, :617, :748-814; godot-client/project-sovereign/scripts/enemy_phase_dialog.gd:470-503; verified by running grep 'random.seed(' backend/ (0 hits); docs/audits/playtest_digests/audit-latewar-t20/digest.md:112-115.
findings.repro: Load tests/fixtures/playtest_saves/fixture_t20_ambient.json with the driver (`--from-save … --turns 8 --script tools/playtest_scripts/diplomacy_latewar.json`) and read the ⚔ tails of any turn with 3+ attacks on one marshal; or call `_pick_observation` twice with identical inputs and observe different/identical picks with no state change.
findings.fix_shape: ONE seam: pick by index `(world.battle_counts.get(pair_key,0)) % len(bank)` through a small `_rotate(bank, key)` helper in `_pick_observation`, the XR-5 idiom, passing the existing `battle_result` pair key.
findings.behaviour_test: tests/test_marshal_voice_tier1.py (or a new battle_report test): two consecutive battles between the same pair with the same outcome yield two different observations from the same bank, and the sequence is byte-identical across two builds with the same `campaign_seed`.
findings.already_filed: none (XR-5 covered enemy_voice banks only).

refuters.reason:
The mechanism as described (unseeded `random.choice`, no `random.seed` anywhere in backend/, and the resulting verbatim repeat) is CONFIRMED by direct reproduction: `_pick_observation` (battle_report.py:617) and its ~30 call sites (e.g. :838 for the exact bank hit) all use bare `random.choice(_OBSERVATIONS[bank])`; `grep -rn "random.seed(" backend/` returns zero hits; and the cited digest lines are real — docs/audits/playtest_digests/audit-latewar-t20/digest.md:112 and :115 both read verbatim "The hills were ours, but Archduke Charles took them. Massena's position was overrun." within the same enemy phase (turn-28's opening phase, grouped under the "## Turn 27" heading by the digest's own command-issued convention — a labeling nuance, not a factual error). The render site is also correct: enemy_phase_dialog.gd:494 (inside the cited 492-495 range) prints `Berthier: "" + observation + ""`. Not already filed — grepped docs/BUG_FIXES.md and docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md; only sibling row XR-5 (BUG_FIXES.md:2995, CLOSED) exists, and it explicitly scoped its fix to `enemy_voice.py`'s named/personality banks, leaving `battle_report.py`'s `_OBSERVATIONS` banks untouched — this is a genuinely new gap, not a duplicate.

However, the `fix_shape` misdiagnoses the seam and invents machinery that doesn't exist. There is no "pair key" anywhere in the codebase for this rotation: `world.battle_counts` is keyed by REGION NAME only (world_state.py:1247 `self.battle_counts: Dict[str, int] = {}`; :4550-4551 `count = battle_counts.get(region_name, 0) + 1`), and the existing deterministic-rotation helper the finding should point at is `_voice_rotation_key(world, region_name)` (combat_executor.py:257-266), already used by BOTH `enemy_voice` (:6307-6311) and the marshal-voice mirror (:6338) — reusing that helper, not inventing a `_rotate(bank, key)` keyed on a nonexistent pair id, is the correct idiom to share.

More importantly, `_pick_observation`/`generate_battle_report` cannot reach `world` or a region name "in `_pick_observation`" as the fix proposes, by design. `generate_battle_report()` is called from INSIDE `backend/game_logic/combat.py`'s `CombatResolver.resolve_battle()` (combat.py:193, call sites at :1022 and :1463) — a method whose signature (attacker, defender, terrain, flanking_bonus, ...) carries no `world` and no region-name parameter at all. battle_report.py itself documents this as deliberate: `compose_campaign_cost_note`'s docstring (battle_report.py ~1010-1013) states "`generate_battle_report` itself has no world access by design — this helper takes the world and is glued on at the combat executor's after-action seam" — i.e. the established pattern in this exact file is to compute world-dependent content ONE LAYER UP in combat_executor.py and glue it onto the result dict afterward, exactly as `enemy_voice` already does. So "a small `_rotate(bank, key)` helper in `_pick_observation`" is not a self-contained one-line change; it either requires threading a rotation key down through the world-independent `resolve_battle()` signature (touching a module deliberately kept independent of `world`), or restructuring `_pick_observation` to expose which bank it selected (not just the filled string) so the SAME `_voice_rotation_key(world, target_location)` value already computed at combat_executor.py:6307 can override the index at the executor glue seam — mirroring the enemy_voice/campaign_cost_note precedent instead of duplicating it with a new keying scheme.

findings.title: Every question dumps the whole COMMAND REFERENCE — "where is Mack?" / "who is at Swabia?" / "what is Davout doing?" get help text although `status` already answers them
findings._corrected: DUPLICATE of CR-8/CR-6 (COMMAND_ROBUSTNESS_SPEC.md:57 and :317-319): backend/ai/llm_client.py:1258 routing every question to `help` is a documented, INTENTIONAL, gated design decision, not an overlooked join — the spec states verbatim that a question-answering Berthier (CR-8's advisory desk, or CR-6's classifier) is what replaces the `help` route, and both sit behind their own USER DESIGN GATE, still unbuilt. Verified live: all 7 repro questions ('where is Mack?' through 'should Ney attack Mack?') do return the COMMAND REFERENCE text; 'can Ney attack Mack' (no '?') fires a real attack confirm; 'will Ney attack Mack?' is excluded from is_question by design (comment at clause_guards.py:282) and is parsed as an order, but hits a region-not-found resolution error rather than literally starting a battle. The proposed fix_shape (blanket-route any name-bearing question to `status`) is too coarse to be the right seam even as an interim patch: `status` has no fortification field ('is Mack fortified?' unanswered) and is a raw data dump with no reasoning ('should Ney attack Mack?' / 'can Ney reach Munich this turn?' unanswered) — three of the finding's own seven examples are advisory/feasibility questions status cannot resolve, which is precisely the gap CR-8's fuller 'mirror diplomatic_advisory.py' design already targets. No new finding to file; if the user wants an interim scoped fix ahead of the CR-8 gate, it should be proposed as a narrower CR-8 sub-slice (pure location lookups only), not a generic 'question names an entity → dump status' rule.
findings.summary: llm_client.py:1258-1272 (verified by opening): `if is_question(original_text): return ParseResult(… action="help", interpretation="Question — showing the command reference")`. The doctrine (a question is not an order) is right, but the answer is the least useful one the game has: the intel report (`status`), the map summary and the diplomatic advisory (`Talleyrand, what does Prussia want?` → relations/strength data, verified by running) all hold the answer.
findings.player_consequence: Verified by running: `where is Mack?`, `who is at Swabia?`, `what is Davout doing?`, `is Mack fortified?`, `how far is Vienna from Ney?`, `Ney, can you reach Munich this turn?`, `should Ney attack Mack?` → all print '═══ COMMAND REFERENCE ═══ MILITARY COMMANDS: attack…'. Meanwhile `can Ney attack Mack` (no '?') and `will Ney attack Mack?` are executed as attacks — so the only difference between getting a manual and starting a battle is a question mark and an auxiliary verb.
findings.evidence: verified by opening backend/ai/llm_client.py:1254-1272 and backend/ai/clause_guards.py `is_question`; verified by running the /command probes (help text vs MUSTER).
findings.repro: POST /command {"command":"where is Mack?"} → message begins with the COMMAND REFERENCE; {"command":"will Ney attack Mack?"} → a battle.
findings.fix_shape: Cheap join at the same seam: when `is_question` fires AND the sentence names a known marshal/enemy/region, return action `status` (or the intel report filtered to that name) instead of `help`; keep `help` for questions naming nothing. The CR-8 two-way channel remains the full answer.
findings.behaviour_test: `where is Mack?` → action status and a fog-honest line naming Swabia at boot; `how do I attack?` still → help; `will Ney attack Mack?` is treated as a question (no battle).
findings.already_filed: CR-8 two-way channel, HELD (COMMAND_ROBUSTNESS_SPEC.md:57) — this is the zero-LLM join available today

refuters.reason:
The mechanism is verified exactly as described. I opened backend/ai/llm_client.py:1258 (`if is_question(original_text): ... action="help"`) and backend/ai/clause_guards.py:284-322 (is_question), then ran all nine repro strings through the real /command endpoint (TestClient with the world/parser swapped per the documented pattern, WorldState.from_scenario on europe_1805.json, mock parser). Confirmed: 'where is Mack?', 'who is at Swabia?', 'what is Davout doing?', 'is Mack fortified?', 'how far is Vienna from Ney?', 'Ney, can you reach Munich this turn?', and 'should Ney attack Mack?' all returned the COMMAND REFERENCE text (action=help). 'can Ney attack Mack' (no '?') fired a real MUSTER/attack confirm. 'will Ney attack Mack?' did NOT hit the help route (confirming the deliberate `will`/`would`/`shall` exclusion documented at clause_guards.py:282-283) but was parsed as an attack order that failed on target resolution ('Region "Mack" not found') — so the repro's 'starts a battle' framing is a mild overstatement (it hits a resolution error, not a fired battle), but the core claim (question mark + excluded auxiliary flips help-vs-order) holds.

However this is not an unnoticed tie-in: it is an EXPLICIT, OWNED, GATED design decision. docs/COMMAND_ROBUSTNESS_SPEC.md:317-319 states verbatim: '6. A question routes to `help`, after diplomatic routing. Talleyrand's advisory desk answers a question better than the command reference does and keeps precedence. A question-answering Berthier is CR-6's to build; when it exists, it replaces the `help` route, not the guard.' The owner row is CR-8 'Two-way channel (questions, not just orders)' at spec line 57 ('military-side advisory mirroring diplomatic_advisory.py; deterministic fog-respecting data ... HELD for CR-8 ... re-confirm at its own review'), cross-referenced from CLAUDE.md's Command Robustness section. Per the task's own kind taxonomy, 'known, owned deferrals... are NOT findings' — this satisfies Golden Rule 9's owner-row/spec/completion-definition bar (CR-8/CR-6, USER DESIGN GATE, completion = 'replaces the help route').

The fix_shape is also imprecise as the RIGHT seam: I ran `status` (the intel report) and confirmed it DOES answer 'where is Mack?'/'who is at Swabia?'/'what is Davout doing?' reasonably (RECENT REPORTS: 'Mack: large force near Swabia'; YOUR FORCES lists Davout's location/troops/stance). But `status` has no fortification field, so it would NOT answer 'is Mack fortified?', and it is a raw data dump with no reasoning, so it would NOT answer 'should Ney attack Mack?' or 'Ney, can you reach Munich this turn?' at all — three of the finding's own seven repro questions are advisory/feasibility questions that a blanket 'route to status' patch does not actually resolve. That's exactly the CR-8 gap the spec already names ('deterministic fog-respecting data' is only half of what CR-8 promises; the advisory/feasibility half needs the fuller mirror-of-diplomatic_advisory build CR-8 already owns). Shipping the proposed heuristic today would be a symptom patch on a subset of the question space, not the seam the project has already decided owns this (and CR-6-adjacent free-text classification features are explicitly gated behind USER DESIGN GATE per CLAUDE.md).

findings.title: The Ledger economy tab's Net omits the Materiel bill — the only component the applied identity needs, and the ledger screen has no row for it
findings._corrected: DUPLICATE-IN-SUBSTANCE of N11/PT-C4 (docs/BUG_FIXES.md:1399, tier-2-landed per :1360; docs/PLAYTEST_FIXES_SPEC.md:242 "not fully closed"), narrowed to the one surface that fix left untouched. `backend/game_logic/dispatch.py:2271-2290` already fixed the identical gap for the Morning Dispatch by calling `_build_economy` in APPLIED mode and labeling the result `treasury_delta_label = "by the accounts"`, with an explicit comment that the EC-W3 Materiel bill is "charged outside Net by design (the plunder-gold precedent)" — a deliberate, tested exclusion (`tests/test_economy_ledger_reconciliation.py:57-75`'s `NET_GOLD_COMPONENTS` guard), not an oversight. The Strategic Ledger screen (`backend/game_logic/ledger.py:56` `_build_economy(world, player)` with no income_data — ALWAYS pure projection, confirmed by reading `_build_economy`'s signature/docstring at `ledger.py:244-252`) never got the same applied-mode call or disclaimer, so `strategic_ledger.gd` renders a bare "Net:" (line 530) with zero materiel awareness (grep-confirmed 0 hits) and no caveat that it is a forward projection, unlike its dispatch sibling. Fix shape: change `build_strategic_ledger` (ledger.py:56) to pass the applied `income_data` for the just-processed turn (mirroring dispatch.py:2274-2277) and add the same "materiel charged at the battle, not in the accounts" disclaimer line to `strategic_ledger.gd`'s economy render — do NOT add materiel into `NET_GOLD_COMPONENTS`/Net itself, which would violate the pinned reconciliation-guard invariant that intentionally keeps it outside Net.
findings.summary: Measured identity: treasury delta == _build_economy(applied).net − materiel_spent_this_turn on all four probed turns (+1701 = 1980−279; +1966 = 1966−0; +1764 = 2131−367; +1932 = 2472−540). The Butcher's Bill is charged outside Net by design (combat_executor.py:2820-2840) and the end-turn banner names it (meta_executor.py:331), but ledger.py:_build_economy has no materiel field and strategic_ledger.gd has no Materiel line (grep verified: zero hits), so the ECONOMY tab's Net over-states the turn's real change by 15-25% on every fighting turn.
findings.player_consequence: The player opens the ledger, reads 'Net +2,131', ends the turn and finds the chest up 1,764; nothing on that screen explains the 367 (the banner does, once, in a scrolling terminal). Over a 24-turn fighting campaign the gap compounds into thousands of gold the ledger never accounted for.
findings.evidence: Verified by running (scratch snippet over TestClient, 4 turns): delta/applied-ledger-net/materiel printed above; projection read at turn start off by +91..+141 from the real delta. Verified by opening: combat_executor.py:2826-2840 (`world.nation_gold[m_nation] -= bill`, tally in materiel_spent_this_turn), meta_executor.py:308-352 (banner's Materiel), ledger.py:244-490 (no materiel key), godot-client/project-sovereign/scripts/strategic_ledger.gd (no 'materiel').
findings.repro: Boot backend.main under LLM_MODE=mock, POST /command 'end turn' three times; each turn compare nation_gold['France'] delta with _build_economy(world,'France',income_data=world._income_phase_results['France'])['net'] and world.materiel_spent_this_turn['France'].
findings.fix_shape: ONE seam: _build_economy returns `materiel` (read from world.materiel_spent_this_turn in applied mode, 0 in projection mode) as a signed informational line; strategic_ledger.gd renders 'Materiel (last turn): -Ng' under Net with the note that it is charged at the battle, not in the accounts.
findings.behaviour_test: After one fought turn, _build_economy(world, player, income_data=applied)['materiel'] equals world.materiel_spent_this_turn[player], and treasury delta == net − materiel exactly.
findings.already_filed: CA9-N11 (BUG_FIXES.md:1399) / PT-C4 (dispatch.py:2276-2291 'by the accounts'). NEW: the ledger economy tab has no Materiel row at all; the exact identity is verified.

refuters.reason: The narrow code fact is real (grep-confirmed: zero "materiel" hits in ledger.py and strategic_ledger.gd) but the finding mischaracterizes it as an undiscovered defect when it is the documented, still-open remainder of an already-landed fix (N11/PT-C4), and its fix_shape/repro rest on a mechanism error: GET /ledger's `_build_economy` call is ALWAYS in pure-projection mode, never "applied" mode, so a materiel field added the way described would read 0 on the actual screen. (1) `backend/game_logic/dispatch.py:2271-2290` shows N11/PT-C4 was already fixed by making the morning-dispatch treasury_delta call `_build_economy(..., income_data=world._income_phase_results.get(player))` (applied mode) and adding an explicit disclaimer: `treasury_delta_label = "by the accounts"` (line 2290), with the comment "PT-C4: CA9-N11 is not fully closed... The EC-W3 Butcher's Bill is charged outside Net by design (the plunder-gold precedent)... The banner now names Materiel inside its own window. This surface says what it is instead of claiming to be an observation." (2) `docs/BUG_FIXES.md:1399` (the row, plain "N11", not "CA9-N11") and `:1360` ("Tier 2... F8's copy half + F5 + N11") show this exact recommendation — "Give [Materiel] a named component, or make both surfaces measure" (`docs/PLAYTEST_FIXES_SPEC.md:242`) — was already identified and half-landed; the finding's own already_filed citation ("CA9-N11 (BUG_FIXES.md:1399)") is wrong in both the id string and in claiming it as merely a related precedent rather than the direct, still-open source of this exact recommendation. (3) `tests/test_economy_ledger_reconciliation.py:57-75` shows a standing, tested `NET_GOLD_COMPONENTS` reconciliation-guard invariant that deliberately and explicitly EXCLUDES materiel from Net (mirroring the "plunder-gold precedent" — outside Net by design) — this is not an accidental omission, it is a pinned contract. (4) `backend/game_logic/ledger.py:56` (`"economy": _build_economy(world, player)`, no income_data arg) proves the real GET /ledger screen is ALWAYS pure-projection, unlike dispatch.py's applied-mode call — so the finding's "applied-ledger-net" numeric identity, obtained by manually passing `income_data=world._income_phase_results['France']` in a scratch script, does not describe what a player ever sees on the real Ledger screen, and the fix_shape's "read from world.materiel_spent_this_turn in applied mode, 0 in projection mode" would render 0 on the shipped screen unless `build_strategic_ledger` is ALSO changed to prefer applied income_data for the CURRENT turn — a second seam the finding never names. The correct, narrower fix is: extend dispatch.py's already-landed pattern (applied-mode _build_economy call + "by the accounts"-style disclaimer) to the Strategic Ledger's economy tab specifically, i.e. change `build_strategic_ledger` (ledger.py:56) to pass `income_data=(getattr(world,'_income_phase_results',None) or {}).get(player)` and add the same Materiel-outside-Net disclaimer/line to strategic_ledger.gd — not "add materiel as a NET_GOLD_COMPONENTS-style component," which would break the pinned reconciliation-guard test's intentional exclusion.

findings.title: Britain guards the Channel against a descent that can no longer happen — the blockade lever is switched off by a spent camp
findings._corrected: REFUTED: naval.py:1537-1557 (`derive_ai_postures`) and naval.py:1560-1588 (`_readiness_tick`) both do exactly what NAVAL_SPEC.md documents as intentional — persistent guard while a camp stands is the deliberately-closed 'oscillation hole' (§5.3.2, NAVAL_SPEC.md:359-360), and any blockade-postured fleet ticking to ceiling 100 regardless of target is rule 1 of §3.3 (NAVAL_SPEC.md:165, 75), unconditional by design and historically grounded (Cornwallis/Nelson). The NAVY_DRILL_CEILING=75 the finding cites only ever applied to non-blockading ('guard') postures (NAVAL_SPEC.md:174), so 'past the 75 ceiling NAVAL_SPEC promises' is a misreading, not a violated promise. Camp_turns is also fully reversible each turn (naval.py:1591-1619 resets it to 0 once camped strength drops), so nothing is 'neutralised for the rest of the war' — it lasts exactly as long as the player's own choice to keep the army camped, which is the intended two-front trade-off the spec names as player-exploitable. No code change is warranted without a design ruling to actually change this behavior.
findings.summary: `derive_ai_postures` flips an island fleet to guard whenever an enemy camp is staged or a window is live, without asking whether the descent is still possible. After the diversion was spent (turn 5) and the Combined Fleet halved (ratio 0.32), 73k Frenchmen sitting at Normandy kept Britain on guard from turn 7 through the end of the run, so `blockade_broken` fired for France, Holland and Spain, their trade recovered, and France's fleet — on 'blockade' posture pinning only fleetless Austria — drilled 50→84, past the 75 ceiling NAVAL_SPEC §5.3.2 promises ('only to the war drill ceiling of 75').
findings.player_consequence: The RN's main weapon (rot + halved trade for three treasuries) is neutralised for the rest of the war by an army that cannot cross; the AI plays measurably worse than the spec intends and the 75-ceiling safeguard is bypassed by taking blockade posture against an empty harbour.
findings.evidence: Verified by opening backend/game_logic/naval.py:1537-1557 (`derive_ai_postures`: camp_turns ≥2 or window_turns >0 → guard; no read of diversion_used or of any crossing ratio) and :1578-1579 (posture=='blockade' and at war → ceiling 100), docs/NAVAL_SPEC.md:355-360 (§5.3.2 'only to the war drill ceiling of 75'). Verified by running: the archived run's t7/t10/t13 snapshots show Britain posture 'guard', `__naval__.blockaded == ['Austria']`, France diversion_used=True, camp_turns 3/6/9, France readiness 55/69/84, `blockade_broken` France/Holland/Spain at turn 7, and `crossing_check(France, Normandy→London)` at t13 = shut 0.32; on a fresh boot with Britain on guard, France on blockade posture (pinning Austria 0 ships + Russia) ticks 74→79 while on guard it ticks 74→75.
findings.repro: 1805 boot: stack ≥40k in Flanders/Artois/Normandy/Brittany, spend the diversion (fail it), end turns — Britain stays on guard indefinitely and the Blockade Board empties of France/Spain/Holland.
findings.fix_shape: ONE seam: in `derive_ai_postures` (naval.py:1548-1556) flip to guard only for a LIVE threat — `window_turns > 0`, or camp staged AND the enemy's `diversion_used` is False AND its hypothetical-window `crossing_check` ratio ≥ WINDOW_CROSSING_FLOOR; (secondary, `_readiness_tick`:1578) grant the 100 ceiling only when `blockade_forecast(world, nation)['closes']` contains a court with ships > 0.
findings.behaviour_test: Staged French camp + `diversion_used=True` + hopeless ratio → after `derive_ai_postures` Britain's posture is 'blockade' and France stays in `blockaded_nations`; staged camp + diversion unspent at boot readiness → 'guard'. Secondary: France on blockade posture pinning only Austria ticks to at most 75 while a superior hostile fleet exists.
findings.already_filed: none — §5.3.2 designs the flip and calls the lapse exploitable; the spent-card blindness and the 75-ceiling bypass are new

refuters.reason:
Both halves of the claimed mechanism are real code behavior but neither is a defect — both are explicit, deliberately-designed rules the spec states in plain prose and defends with reasoning, so the finding mischaracterizes intended design as an AI blind spot / broken promise.

(1) `derive_ai_postures` (naval.py:1537-1557, verified by reading) does exactly what the finding describes mechanically: it flips an island nation to 'guard' whenever ANY enemy's `camp_turns >= DESCENT_CAMP_STAGED_TURNS` (2) OR `window_turns > 0`, with no read of `diversion_used` or any crossing ratio. But NAVAL_SPEC.md:355-360 documents this as deliberate: '2. Britain reacts (derived, §6): posture flips blockade→guard... Consequence the player can exploit: the blockade of Brest/Toulon LAPSES... the two-front tension is automatic, no scripting, and waiting alone can never open the Strait (v1.0.3 — the oscillation hole is closed).' The spec explicitly frames the blockade-lapse as a player-exploitable STRATEGIC OPPORTUNITY, not an AI failure, and explicitly records that a prior version DID revert to blockade prematurely and that this was a bug ('the oscillation hole') that v1.0.3 deliberately closed by making guard persist for the whole camp's duration. The finding's proposed fix would reopen exactly the hole the spec says was closed. Also, `_camp_tick` (naval.py:1591-1619, verified by reading) resets `camp_turns` to 0 the moment camped strength drops below `DESCENT_CAMP_MIN_TROOPS`, so Britain's guard posture re-derives every turn from current state — 'neutralised for the rest of the war' is false; it lasts only as long as the player chooses to keep the army camped, which is the intended two-front trade-off (guard lifts the blockade in exchange for the invasion staying live).

(2) `_readiness_tick` (naval.py:1560-1588, verified by reading) does give ANY posture=='blockade' fleet a ceiling of 100 unconditionally while at war, regardless of who it targets or whether a superior hostile fleet exists — confirmed against docs/NAVAL_SPEC.md:165 ('Blockading fleet: holds 100 (sea time drills crews)') and :75 (H2: 'Cornwallis off Brest and Nelson off Toulon kept RN crews at sea and drilled... Readiness: blockading fleet holds 100'). This is rule 1 of §3.3, stated as unconditional and historically grounded; the 'war drill ceiling of 75' the finding cites (NAVAL_SPEC.md:174, 'Otherwise: +5/turn — toward NAVY_DRILL_CEILING=75') is explicitly scoped to non-blockading ('guard') postures only. So a fleet on blockade posture reaching 100 is not 'past the ceiling NAVAL_SPEC promises' — it never carried that promise. I additionally confirmed `set_fleet_posture` (backend/commands/naval_executor.py:78-106, verified by reading) lets ANY nation, island or not, set posture='blockade' with no gate, and `blockader_against` (naval.py:346-368) makes the untargeted blockade trivially pin a fleetless at-war nation, matching the finding's 'pinning only fleetless Austria' description exactly — this part of the finding is mechanically accurate, but it is an INDEPENDENT mechanism from claim (1) (France's own posture choice, unrelated to Britain's derived posture) that the finding wrongly wove into a single causal chain ('so France's fleet... drilled 50→84, past the 75 ceiling'), and it is not a bug either since §3.3 unconditionally grants blockade postures the 100 ceiling by design, with the explicit trade-off named in the executor's own message: 'Our own coasts go unguarded.'

The fix_shape for both seams would directly contradict documented, reasoned design (re-opening the closed 'oscillation hole'; and adding a 'closes a court with ships>0' gate to a rule the spec states unconditionally). already_filed is correctly 'none' (no BUG_FIXES/DESIGN_REFINEMENT row matches), but that is because there is nothing here to file — this is working as designed, not an unowned defect.

findings.title: Conquests are never held: the AI cannot garrison a fresh capture, so provinces ping-pong and a 4,700-man corps walks sixteen French provinces
findings._corrected: DUPLICATE of nothing filed, but the mechanism is wrong: P6.75 `_consider_garrison` (enemy_ai.py:4086-4185) is reachable and DOES fire (5 times in an 8-turn ambient probe, all on long-held home borders like Silesia/Podolia/Lithuania) — the enemy-marshal-adjacent check at :4147-4154 caused 0 of 252 rejections in that probe. The true reasons fresh conquests specifically are never held: (1) P4/P4.25/P4.5 (attack/garrison-assault/capture, :1970-1995) always outrank P6.75 (:2141) within one marshal's single per-turn decision, so a corps that just captured almost always advances again rather than staying; (2) `AI_GARRISON_MIN_STRENGTH = 20000` (:410) excludes small mobile/expeditionary corps entirely — e.g. Paget's ~4,756-man corps in fixture_t20 is ~4x under this floor and could never garrison regardless of adjacency; (3) `GARRISON_MAX_PER_NATION = 3` (economy_executor.py:97) already spends one slot on the pre-garrisoned capital (world_state.py:2415, `get_capital_garrison_target`), a cap shared identically with the player by design (GR8). If this is worth filing, the fix_shape should target the priority ordering (let a marshal who captured this turn re-evaluate garrison before further advance next turn) and/or reconsider whether the 3-cap is too tight for a multi-front AI nation — not the enemy-adjacent clause at :4147-4155, which the evidence shows is not the operative gate.
findings.summary: Capture is instant and un-held. The only AI rung that leaves men behind, P6.75 `_consider_garrison` (enemy_ai.py:4086-4185), requires >=20,000 men (:410), own-controlled soil, no garrison, no enemy in OR adjacent to the region (:4147-4155), no friendly present and a border — conditions a fresh conquest can never meet (an enemy is adjacent by definition), while the verb itself is a 3,000-man detachment for 2 AP capped at three garrisons per nation including capitals (economy_executor.py:95-97, world_state.py:941). So every conquest is a coin that flips back the moment the corps walks on, and P4.5 keeps re-taking the same provinces.
findings.player_consequence: The war is a province tennis match with no front: Franconia flips Austria↔Bavaria repeatedly (audit-ambient40 Turn 8 and Turn 14 both read `Deroy marches ... into Franconia unopposed! Captured: Austria → Bavaria`; audit-naval Turn 8), Leon is `taken by Britain` twice in ambient40 (Turns 6, 11) and twice in flagship-mock, Aragon flips at naval Turns 11/13 and Spain re-takes Leon with `Castanos marches from Leon into Leon unopposed!` (Turn 14); the enemy-phase dialog repeats the same conquest line turn after turn; and because nothing can be left behind, Paget's 4,756-man corps (fixture_t20) walks 16 French provinces at three a turn (audit-latewar-t20 Turns 20-28) with France's own retake equally free. A Paradox player expects an occupied province to need something to hold it.
findings.evidence: Verified by opening: enemy_ai.py:4086-4185 (every condition listed), :410 `AI_GARRISON_MIN_STRENGTH = 20000`, economy_executor.py:95 `GARRISON_DETACHMENT_SIZE = 3000`, :97 `GARRISON_MAX_PER_NATION = 3`, world_state.py:941 `"garrison": 2`. Digest lines quoted verbatim from audit-ambient40 Turns 8/14, audit-naval Turns 8/11/13/14, audit-latewar-t20 Turns 20-28; fixture_t20 (verified by opening) shows Paget at Berry with 4,756 men and every non-capital French province ungarrisoned.
findings.repro: Load `tests/fixtures/playtest_saves/fixture_t20_ambient.json`, run `EnemyAI(CommandExecutor())._consider_garrison(w.marshals['Deroy'],'Bavaria',w)` after standing Deroy (9,218 men) on a freshly captured border province with an enemy corps adjacent → None on every branch (strength, enemy adjacent); or read audit-latewar-t20 Turns 20-28 for the walk.
findings.fix_shape: Design gate (owner: the next AI/design pass), seam if built = `_consider_garrison`: let P4.5 leave a detachment when the captured border province has an enemy corps within two hops and the capturing corps is at least twice the detachment (relax the no-enemy-adjacent clause at :4147-4155 for fresh conquests, and let the cap exclude capital garrisons) — or introduce an occupation/control timer so an unheld conquest reverts. Either way the same rule must reach the player's `garrison` verb (GR5).
findings.behaviour_test: Shape: Deroy 22,000 captures an enemy border province with an enemy corps two hops away → the nation's next action for Deroy is `garrison` and the province survives the enemy's next unopposed march; control: with the rule disabled the province flips back next phase.
findings.already_filed: None found (grep ping-pong / flips back / unheld in BUG_FIXES.md and DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md); PC15-D4's 'unheld homeland returns at the exit' is the settlement-time cousin, not the field rule.

refuters.reason: The stated causal mechanism does not match what the code does, and I falsified it empirically. I ran an 8-turn ambient probe (`playtest_driver.py --turns 8 --fresh`, AI_DEBUG=1) and captured all 252 `P6.75` evaluations from `tools/playtest_runs/probe-mechanism-garrison2/server_console.log`. The rejection-reason breakdown is: fortified 77, already-garrisoned 58, at-cap-3/3 24, drilling 19, fully-surrounded 18, too-weak(<20k) 50, already-in-region 1 — and ZERO rejections for 'enemy in region' or 'enemy adjacent' (the two branches at enemy_ai.py:4148 and :4151-4154, confirmed by opening the file — line numbers close to the finding's cited 4147-4155). The claim 'conditions a fresh conquest can never meet (an enemy is adjacent by definition)' is a conflation error: the code has TWO independent adjacency checks that are not mutually exclusive — 'no enemy MARSHAL in/adjacent' (:4147-4154, the safety gate) and 'at least one adjacent region is non-friendly CONTROLLED' (:4167-4176, the vulnerability requirement, checking `region.controller`, not marshal presence). A freshly captured border province routinely satisfies both: the enemy's territory is still next door (satisfying vulnerability) while no enemy corps happens to be standing on it right now (satisfying safety). My probe proves the AI DOES place garrisons via P6.75 — 5 times in 8 turns (Hohenlohe→Silesia, Kutuzov→Podolia x2, Buxhowden→Lithuania x2, all confirmed by `[AI GARRISON] ... (strength ..., border region)` lines in the console log) — so the rung is reachable and does fire; it just fires on long-held home borders, not on same-turn fresh conquests, because P4/P4.25/P4.5 (attack/garrison-assault/capture, enemy_ai.py:1970-1995) structurally outrank P6.75 (:2141) in the SAME marshal's decision this turn, so a corps that just captured almost always marches on rather than staying — that ordering, not the enemy-adjacency check, is why fresh conquests specifically don't get held. The finding's own flagship example is also mis-attributed: Paget's cited '4,756-man corps' (fixture_t20) is roughly 4x BELOW `AI_GARRISON_MIN_STRENGTH = 20000` (enemy_ai.py:410, confirmed by opening), so he could never garrison ANYTHING regardless of what's adjacent — the strength floor alone fully explains that example, with the enemy-adjacency clause never in play. Because the diagnosed mechanism is wrong, the fix_shape (relax the no-enemy-adjacent clause at :4147-4155) targets a seam that is essentially never the actual blocker (0/252 in an 8-turn sample) and would be a no-op against the real bottleneck, which is the priority ordering (garrison never outranks continuing to advance) compounded by the 3-garrison-per-nation cap (economy_executor.py:97, confirmed) that already consumes one slot on the capital alone (confirmed: capitals boot pre-garrisoned via `get_capital_garrison_target`, world_state.py:2415, matching the observed 'already garrisoned (25,000)' rejections) — a structural, GR8/Building-Blocks-shared limit the player faces identically, arguably by design rather than by defect. The province-flip symptom itself (Franconia, Leon, Aragon, Paget's march) is real and independently verified in the digests, but a correct finding about it would name the priority-ordering + cap-and-floor interaction as the mechanism, not an 'impossible enemy-adjacent' condition that the code and a live run both show is essentially never hit.

working_well.title: Working well: petitions arrive with honest arms — non-AP gates keep their reason, AP-only gates are re-derived at delivery
working_well.summary: The lens question 'are petitions arriving with disabled arms?' is answered No by construction: `_command_option` bakes `available: False` + `unavailable_reason` for a non-AP refusal (jealousy.py:1779-1795) while `refresh_petition_affordability` (1870-1950) is subtractive and re-derives only `ap_cost` arms against live AP at the delivery seam (main.py:1657-1659), and a refused answer hands back the refreshed card rather than destroying it (2560-2575). The IGR-2 P1 (arms baked at zero AP before `advance_turn` refilled) and the PT-A1 over-correction are both closed and the split is legible in the code.

working_well.title: Working well: the Marshalate closes the roster loop — a lost marshal's name routes to the bench only when the commission gate would pass, and the AI commissions unprompted

working_well.summary: Table (store → round-trips → raised at load): tactical objection `world.pending_objection` (world_state.py:6928/:7527) → yes → NO, deliberate (see the WO-35 row; the executor block names the answer words, executor.py:961-991). Strategic objection `pending_strategic_objection` (:6930/:7529) → yes → NO, but it blocks nothing and LAPSES at the boundary with a told `strategic_objection_lapsed` event (:9337-9370, WO-38). Clarification `command_clarification` (dialogue_manager current, :7180/:7702) → yes → NO; the next typed line consumes it (main.py:2157-2175) and `clear_stale` drops it at the boundary (dialogue_manager.py:691-746); typed `save` clears it (interpret→pass→pop) and the modal gate blocks pause-menu saves, so a save cannot carry it. Interrupt `marshal.pending_interrupt` (marshal.py:1682/:1874) → yes → YES, first standing player marshal (main.py:4123-4129, hazard-4 guard). Capture `pending_capture_choice` (:6931/:7530) → yes → YES (main.py:4098-4100; plunder price backfilled :7536-7547). Redemption `pending_redemption` (:6929/:7528) → yes → YES via `standing_redemption` (disobedience.py:663-687, main.py:4139-4142). Petition `pending_marshal_petition` (:6934/:7549-7554 re-pushes the PopupQueue) → yes → rides the FIRST /command (main.py:4084 fills without draining; :1642 pops with AP re-derived :1671-1676). Incoming proposal / settlement offer / coalition / sabotage / rebellion / proclamation / objection / result / paradox popups (all 10 PRIORITY_ORDER slots, cooldown_manager.py:145-163, each with a serialized property :7280-7290/:8150-8203) → yes → rides the first /command (:1683-1699 safety valve for a proposal in the dialogue slot). HARD_STOP dialogues (war_purpose_selection, settlement_confirm, commitment_paradox; dialogue_manager.py:66-82) → yes → NOT at load, but the first typed command is refused with the numbered options and the refusal carries `diplomatic_dialogue`, which the client re-mounts (main.py:2628-2672; main.gd:2366-2372). Glorious charge `marshal.pending_glorious_charge` (marshal.py:1725/:1927) → yes → NO raise; the next bare `charge` resolves it (combat_executor.py:7532-7535); unreachable in a save (modal, no close: glorious_charge_dialog.gd:125/131; pause gated main.gd:992/:5380; end turn not blocked but the popup is).

working_well.title: NV-5's Peninsular shape fires unprompted: Britain lands at Lisbon and Spain fights back
working_well.summary: With no script driving Britain, Paget was commissioned at London, put ashore at Lisbon (Portugal, the host at relation 40) on turn 5 with 5,000 men, took Leon (T6), Asturias (T7), Bordelais (T10), Aragon and Toledo, and Spain's Castanos brought him to battle at Aragon on turns 11/13/14 and retook Leon — the 1808 story the NV-5 landing record promised, in miniature, while Moore's 30k stayed home over the lift. (Note for the map lens: Galicia→Bordelais is a registry LAND edge with no sea link — `Galicia.adjacent` contains Bordelais, `naval.is_sea_link` is False — so the walk from Lisbon reaches French soil across the Bay of Biscay without ever meeting the crossing gate.)

working_well.title: The /load re-attach discipline is coherent end to end, and every pending question is now classified (table)
working_well.summary: `/load` re-attaches the capture question (main.py:4086-4089), a STANDING marshal's interrupt with the tombstone guard (:4104-4111) and the redemption via the ONE liveness predicate (:4131-4137); the client raises them through the SAME predicates the command path uses with capture→interrupt→redemption precedence (main.gd:4634-4680); from_dict re-primes the petition slot (world_state.py:7558-7560) and sweeps stale rebellion popups (8156-8185); `_fill_popup_keys_without_draining` (main.py:1509-1529) keeps the queue intact so nothing is lost. Table (round-trips / raised at /load / raised on the first command after): tactical objection — yes / no (deliberate, main.py:4114) / no, refusal text names the answer words, unreachable from the client · strategic objection — yes / no / blocks nothing, lapses at the next boundary with a told event (world_state.py:9302-9334) · clarification — yes / no / no, silently consumes a bare name (finding above) · marshal interrupt — yes / YES · capture choice — yes / YES · redemption — yes / YES · marshal petition — yes, queue re-primed / no (key filled None) / YES on the 1st command · incoming proposal or ultimatum — yes / no / YES (2nd command, below the petition in priority; the mailbox badge counts it at load) · incoming settlement offer — yes / no / YES (3rd) · HARD_STOP dialogue (war_purpose_selection) — yes / no / YES, the first command is refused and the refusal carries `diplomatic_dialogue` (main.py:2657-2671 → main.gd:2366-2380 modal) · glorious charge — yes (marshal field) / no / a bare `charge` fires it (combat_executor.py:7531-7534), unreachable from the client · sabotage/coalition/proclamation/paradox/rebellion popups — yes / no / YES via the queue, one per response.

working_well.title: Working well: the alliance-paradox block arrives disabled at mount with its reason AND two named routes
working_well.summary: The BPH-C paradox no longer dead-ends silently: the `proposal_confirm` mount disables `execute_proposal` and sets `unavailable_reason` = 'I cannot deliver this, Sire — Making peace with Austria while allied with Bavaria (who is still at war with Austria) creates a diplomatic contradiction. Settle the war jointly at the settlement table, or resolve Bavaria's war first.' while modify/adjust/reconsider stay live (diplomatic_dialogue.py:858-898), the send gate is a second line of defence (diplomatic_executor.py:3919-3936), and the Godot popup renders the disabled state with the reason as tooltip (proposal_confirm_popup.gd:212-224). Verified at boot by running. (The two named routes lead into findings 1 and 6 — the honesty is right, the destinations are broken.)

working_well.title: Working well: the peace vocabulary is coherent — 'offer peace', 'propose peace', 'request terms' each resolve to the right instrument and the redirects explain themselves
working_well.summary: `offer peace to Austria` (audit-flagship-mock T18) and `propose peace with Austria` (audit-propose T1) both parse to the Peace Treaty proposal_confirm; `Talleyrand, request terms from Austria` under a coalition war explains the substitution ('Austria fights under Britain's lead in …, Sire — the coalition's terms are the leader's to name, not each court's own. I shall ask Britain's chancery to speak for their alliance.', diplomatic_templates.py:2138-2143, PC15-6 landed) and, when an offer is pending, points at the mailbox (display_names.py:877-884); the war row carries the per-war `request_terms_state` with named clocks ('No court names terms this early in a war, Sire. (2 turns remaining.)', settlement_routes.py:293-316) rather than a click-only refusal. Verified by running `build_active_wars` on the t20 fixture and by the archived digests.

working_well.title: Working well: Mode A determinism is real and auditable — a fresh replay reproduced an archived 24-turn arm byte-for-byte through turn 13, and refusals are printed in the engine's own words
working_well.summary: Verified by running: `playtest_driver.py --turns 13 --diplomacy propose` and diffing against docs/audits/playtest_digests/audit-propose/digest.md — zero differing lines through the turn-13 block, exactly as PLAYTESTING.md promises (the sha256 per-turn reseed at tools/playtest_driver.py:90-96 plus the PYTHONHASHSEED re-exec at :1433-1437, both recorded in meta.json's `rng` block). This is what made every finding above CHECKABLE: the propose replay let me open /pending_envoy at the exact turn the archive went blind. The stale-passthrough guard (`begin_post`/`_answered_dialogue_ids`, :585-612) and the `↳ refused:` note (:920-923) also mean the digests are honest where they look — the flagship's four unanswered offers are visible as '(left standing)' rather than hidden.
